chapters.title: Effects of our Actions on the Environment

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: Can We Do Anything?
lessons.notes_html:
The Story in Short

The story "Can We Do Anything?" is about pollution around us and what we, as citizens and students, can do to stop it. Ali is excited on the first day of school after the long summer vacations because he wants to meet his classmates and teachers. He travels in a van with his best friend Saleem. On the way, the boys talk about their holidays, but loud horns disturb them and the fumes from vehicles enter the van through the windows, so some students start coughing.

In class, Miss Sana shows the students some posters on pollution. The students discuss pollution and admit that they had only been complaining about it — they had done nothing to stop it. The class then works in groups and makes a plan to fight pollution. Ali and his group arrange a campaigning programme in their neighbourhood: they make and show posters, distribute handbills listing the steps young people can take, present role-plays, give speeches and share an action plan for cleaning the neighbourhood. The programme is a big success because almost everyone agrees to do something. Ali comes home tired, but very happy, because he has taken a big step in the right direction.

The Three Sections of the Story

  • Section 1 — Air Pollution: Ali's morning and his journey to school.
  • Section 2 — Pollution Free Environment: the class discussion and the group plan.
  • Section 3 — A Task Completed: the neighbourhood campaign.
  • "Social Hazard" is the extra title that does not belong to any section.

Word Meanings

  • enthusiastic — very excited or interested
  • social campaigns — activities to make people aware about something
  • involved — made them take part
  • honked — blew the horn
  • fumes — dangerous smoke having a strong smell
  • emitted — produced
  • purposeless — without any purpose or reason
  • assign — give (work)
  • deadlines — the dates by which something will be completed
  • tasks — work that has to be done
  • reviewed — checked something to see if any change is needed
  • attendees — people who attend a programme or meeting

Comprehension Key Points

  • Ali liked science because he enjoyed doing experiments, and he eagerly waited for his Social Studies class too.
  • Miss Sana raised her hand as a signal for complete silence and the full attention of the students.
  • Miss Sana challenged her students' minds because she always made them reflect and think in new ways.
  • The handbills about pollution were made by Ali and his friends themselves, not by an advertising agency.
  • As citizens, our responsibility is to keep our surroundings clean, stop pollution, and take part in work that brings a good change.

mcqs.q: What is the story 'Can We Do Anything?' mainly about?
options: A boy's journey to a new school
How to make posters for a competition
The summer vacations of two friends
Pollution around us and what we can do to stop it
mcqs.why: The correct answer is pollution around us and what we can do to stop it. In the pre-reading discussion the book explains that the story is about pollution and the part that citizens and students can play in stopping it. The whole class plan and the neighbourhood campaign in the story grow out of this idea.

mcqs.q: Next to whom did Ali sit in the van?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is his best friend Saleem. The true/false exercise confirms it: the statement 'Ali sat beside the driver uncle in the van' is false, because Ali sat next to Saleem and the two friends talked about their holidays.

mcqs.q: Why did some students cough in the van?
options: The fumes from the vehicles were entering the van through the windows
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that the fumes from the vehicles were entering the van through the windows. In Exercise 6 the book completes the sentence exactly this way. This small detail shows how air pollution affects us in daily life.

mcqs.q: Who showed the posters on pollution to the class?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Miss Sana. The students started discussing pollution because Miss Sana showed them some posters on pollution. Her posters started the whole discussion that led to the class plan.

mcqs.q: What did Miss Sana's raised hand mean in the class?
options: It was her signal for complete silence and full attention
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that it was her signal for complete silence and the full attention of the students. Exercise 6 of the reading section gives this reason, and it shows one of Miss Sana's classroom habits.

mcqs.q: What had the students done to stop pollution before Miss Sana asked them?
options: They had written letters to the government
Nothing — they had only complained about pollution
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that they had done nothing; they kept complaining about pollution but had done nothing to stop it. That is why the classroom fell into pin-drop silence when Miss Sana asked them the question.

mcqs.q: Which title belongs to Section 2 of the story (the class discussion and group plan)?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Pollution Free Environment. In Exercise 1, Section 1 (Ali's morning and journey) matches 'Air Pollution', Section 2 (class discussion and group plan) matches 'Pollution Free Environment', and Section 3 (the neighbourhood campaign) matches 'A Task Completed'.

mcqs.q: Which title in Exercise 1 is extra and does not match any section?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Social Hazard. The story has only three sections, so one of the four titles is extra, and the book's answer names 'Social Hazard' as the extra title.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'fumes' mean?
options: Dangerous smoke having a strong smell
mcqs.why: The correct answer is dangerous smoke having a strong smell. In the matching exercise, 'fumes' is paired with this meaning, and in the story the black fumes from buses and other vehicles pollute the air and make students cough.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'enthusiastic' mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is very excited or interested. The vocabulary exercise matches 'enthusiastic' with this meaning; for example, the students were enthusiastic about the cleanliness campaign.

mcqs.q: What did Ali and his group distribute in the neighbourhood?
options: Handbills listing steps the youth could take
mcqs.why: The correct answer is handbills listing steps the youth could take. In Exercise 7 the book says the group made and showed posters, distributed handbills, presented role-plays, gave speeches and shared an action plan for cleaning their neighbourhood.

mcqs.q: Who made the handbills about pollution?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Ali and his friends themselves. The statement 'The handbills about pollution were made by an advertising agency' is marked false in the book; the students made them with their own hands.

mcqs.q: Why was the neighbourhood programme a big success?
options: Almost everyone agreed to do something to fight pollution
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that almost everyone agreed to do something to fight pollution. Exercise 6 completes the sentence 'The programme was a big success because...' with exactly this reason.

mcqs.q: How did Ali feel after the programme?
options: Fresh and not tired at all
mcqs.why: The correct answer is tired but very happy. The statement 'Ali was not tired at all after the programme' is false; after the whole day's campaigning Ali was tired, yet he was very happy because he had taken a big step in the right direction.

mcqs.q: Why did Ali want to attend the science class?
options: He enjoyed doing experiments during the science lessons
He wanted to meet a new teacher
He had to return a book
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that he enjoyed doing experiments during the science lessons. Exercise 6 completes the statement 'He wanted to attend the science class because...' with this reason, which also shows Ali's interest in learning.

lessons.title: Speaking: Identify a Problem and Propose a Solution
lessons.notes_html:
What We Practise

In section 1.2 we learn to identify a problem and propose a solution. Saleh and Bachal talk about the problem of malaria in their area and suggest practical steps to fight it.

Solutions for Malaria in the Dialogue

  • Educate school children about malaria so that they can protect themselves and guide others.
  • Spray kerosene on stagnant water, because mosquitoes breed in standing water.
  • Cover the body with a thin cloth or a net while sleeping, so mosquitoes cannot bite.
  • Ask the Union Council member to order regular spray in the area.

Using the Same Pattern for Another Topic

For a problem like diarrhoea, pupils brainstorm similar steps:

  • Drink clean water.
  • Wash hands properly, especially before eating.
  • Keep food covered so flies cannot sit on it.

Remember

First name the problem clearly, then propose solutions one by one. A good solution is practical — something people can really do in their homes, school or neighbourhood.

mcqs.q: Which problem do Saleh and Bachal discuss in the speaking dialogue?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is malaria in their area. The speaking section says the dialogue is about identifying a problem and proposing a solution, and the problem chosen in the book's dialogue is malaria.

mcqs.q: According to the dialogue, how can school children help in fighting malaria?
options: By being educated about malaria and spreading awareness
mcqs.why: The correct answer is by being educated about malaria. The model answer says the dialogue proposes fighting malaria first by educating school children, because aware children can protect themselves and guide their families.

mcqs.q: What should be sprayed on stagnant water to fight malaria?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is kerosene. The dialogue proposes spraying kerosene on stagnant (standing) water, because mosquitoes lay eggs in standing water and kerosene stops them from breeding.

mcqs.q: How can people protect themselves from mosquito bites while sleeping?
options: By covering the body with a thin cloth or net
mcqs.why: The correct answer is by covering the body with a thin cloth or a net while sleeping. This is one of the practical steps proposed in Saleh and Bachal's dialogue on malaria.

mcqs.q: Whom should the people ask to order regular spray in the area?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Union Council member. The dialogue suggests asking the Union Council member to order regular spray in the area, because such spraying is arranged by the local council.

mcqs.q: In the same dialogue pattern, which step helps prevent diarrhoea?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is drinking clean water. When the book repeats the dialogue pattern for diarrhoea, the brainstormed steps are clean drinking water, hand-washing and covering food.

mcqs.q: Why should food be kept covered?
options: So that flies cannot sit on it and spread germs
So that children cannot see it
mcqs.why: The correct answer is so that flies cannot sit on it and spread germs. Covering food is one of the steps the book suggests for preventing diarrhoea, together with clean water and hand-washing.

mcqs.q: What is the speaking skill practised in section 1.2?
options: Identifying a problem and proposing a solution
mcqs.why: The correct answer is identifying a problem and proposing a solution. That is the title of section 1.2 in the unit contents, and the Saleh–Bachal dialogue is built exactly on this pattern.

mcqs.q: What should we do first when we use this dialogue pattern?
options: Propose all the solutions at once
Name and identify the problem clearly
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to name and identify the problem clearly. Only after the problem (for example malaria) is clear can the speakers propose sensible solutions, one by one.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a practical solution, like the ones in the dialogue?
options: Waiting for others to clean the area
mcqs.why: The correct answer is spraying kerosene on stagnant water. The book's dialogue proposes practical steps that people can really take; only complaining or doing nothing does not solve any problem.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Possessive Pronouns
lessons.notes_html:
What Are Possessive Pronouns?

Possessive pronouns show that something belongs to someone. They stand alone — they are not followed by a noun.

  • mine — belongs to me: The pictures are all mine.
  • ours — belongs to us: The house is ours.
  • yours — belongs to you: You received this prize. It is yours.
  • his — belongs to him: The car is his.
  • hers — belongs to her: The pencil was hers.
  • its — belongs to it: The food is its.
  • theirs — belongs to them: The goats are theirs.

Important Spelling Point

Possessive pronouns never take an apostrophe. The book's word box prints "our's", "your's", "their's" and "her's" — these are typos in the book. The correct forms are ours, yours, theirs, hers.

Examples from the Exercises

  • "Hers is the blue one." (Meena's bowl of ice-cream)
  • "I like your dress. Do you like mine?" (my dress)
  • "I found Ali's socks but couldn't find yours." (your socks)
  • "All the books were good but his was the best." (Ali's story book)
  • "Here is your car, ours is over there, where we left it." (our family's car)
  • "The dog is wearing a nice collar, but it is not its." (the collar belongs to some other dog)

mcqs.q: This is the cat's food. The food is ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'its'. The food belongs to the cat (an animal, 'it'), so we use the possessive pronoun 'its'. Remember that possessive pronouns stand alone and never take an apostrophe.

mcqs.q: That house belongs to us. The house is ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'ours'. The house belongs to 'us', so the possessive pronoun is 'ours'. The book's box prints 'our's', but that is a typo — possessive pronouns never have an apostrophe.

mcqs.q: Adnan is the owner of the blue car. The car is ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'his'. The car belongs to Adnan (a male), so we use 'his'. 'Him' and 'he' cannot show possession in this way.

mcqs.q: I have many pictures. The pictures are all ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'mine'. The pictures belong to the speaker ('I'), so the possessive pronoun is 'mine'. 'My' must be followed by a noun, but here the pronoun stands alone.

mcqs.q: You received this prize. It is ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'yours'. The prize belongs to 'you'. The form 'your's' printed in the book's box is a typo; possessive pronouns are written without an apostrophe.

mcqs.q: These goats were given to them. The goats are ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'theirs'. The goats belong to 'them', so we use 'theirs'. 'Their' comes before a noun (their goats), while 'theirs' stands alone.

mcqs.q: The teacher gave her the pencil. The pencil was ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'hers'. The pencil belongs to 'her' (a girl/woman), and the pronoun stands alone at the end, so 'hers' is correct. 'Her's' with an apostrophe is a book typo.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is written correctly?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'The book is yours.' Possessive pronouns — mine, ours, yours, his, hers, its, theirs — never take an apostrophe, even though the book's word box prints some of them with one by mistake.

mcqs.q: 'Hers is the blue one.' In the exercise, whose bowl of ice-cream is the blue one?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Meena's. The exercise says: 'Look at the bowls of ice-cream. Hers is the blue one,' and the note tells us the bowl belongs to Meena, so 'hers' refers to Meena.

mcqs.q: I like your dress. Do you like ______?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'mine'. The speaker asks about her own dress, so she uses the possessive pronoun 'mine', which stands alone without a noun after it.

mcqs.q: I looked everywhere for your socks. I found Ali's socks but couldn't find ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'yours'. The missing socks belong to 'you', and because the pronoun stands alone at the end of the sentence, we use 'yours', not 'your'.

mcqs.q: All the books were good but ______ was the best. (Ali's story book)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'his'. The best book was Ali's story book, and Ali is male, so the possessive pronoun is 'his'.

mcqs.q: Here is your car, ______ is over there, where we left it. (our family's car)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'ours'. The car over there belongs to the speaker's family ('us'), so the possessive pronoun 'ours' is used.

mcqs.q: The dog is wearing a nice collar, but it is not ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'its'. The collar belongs to some other dog, not to this one. 'Its' is the possessive pronoun for animals and things, and it is written without an apostrophe (unlike 'it's', which means 'it is').

mcqs.q: Yaqoob says: 'Wow! This computer is ______ now!' (The computer was bought for Yaqoob.)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'mine'. The computer was bought for Yaqoob himself, and Yaqoob is the speaker, so he uses 'mine' for something that belongs to him.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Countable and Uncountable Nouns
lessons.notes_html:
Countable and Uncountable Nouns

Countable nouns can be counted: book, pen, student, chair, apple, car, bird, house, boy, girl, table, dog, ball, school, mango.

Uncountable nouns cannot be counted one by one: water, milk, sugar, rice, air, sand, oil, flour, tea, salt, honey, smoke, music, homework, furniture.

How Much? / How Many?

  • Use How many with countable nouns: How many bananas? — a dozen bananas. How many eggs? — a dozen eggs.
  • Use How much with uncountable nouns: How much meat? — two kilograms of meat. How much oil? — a litre of oil.

Useful Quantity Phrases (from Exercise 5)

  • a glass of water
  • a slice of bread
  • a pinch of salt
  • a sack of flour
  • a spoonful of sugar
  • a lot of traffic
  • a tankful of water
  • three cups of tea
  • some money
  • 10 pages of information

mcqs.q: Which of these nouns is countable?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'book'. We can count books — one book, two books. Water, sugar and air are uncountable nouns in the book's list; we cannot say 'two waters' or 'three sugars'.

mcqs.q: Which of these nouns is uncountable?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'milk'. Milk is a liquid that we measure (a litre of milk) but do not count one by one. Apples, chairs and mangoes are countable nouns.

mcqs.q: Can I have ______ water, please?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'a glass of'. Water is uncountable, so we count it with a container word: a glass of water, a tankful of water.

mcqs.q: Pass me ______ bread, please.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'a slice of'. Bread is uncountable, and we take it in slices: a slice of bread. This is one of the phrase-box answers in Exercise 5.

mcqs.q: Add ______ salt in the flour.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'a pinch of'. Salt is uncountable and only a tiny amount is added, so the book uses 'a pinch of salt' — the amount held between finger and thumb.

mcqs.q: Ahmed carried ______ flour on his back.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'a sack of'. Flour is carried in a large bag called a sack, so the sentence is 'Ahmed carried a sack of flour on his back.'

mcqs.q: Put ______ sugar in my tea.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'a spoonful of'. Sugar for one cup of tea is measured with a spoon: a spoonful of sugar.

mcqs.q: There is ______ traffic on the road.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'a lot of'. 'Traffic' is uncountable, and when the quantity is large and not exact, the book uses 'a lot of traffic'.

mcqs.q: ______ bananas did your mother buy? — A dozen.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'How many'. Bananas are countable, so we ask 'How many bananas?' In the shopping-list exercise the answer is 'a dozen bananas'.

mcqs.q: ______ meat did she buy? — Two kilograms.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'How much'. Meat is uncountable, so we ask 'How much meat?' and answer with a weight: two kilograms of meat.

mcqs.q: In the shopping list, how much oil is bought?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a litre of oil. Oil is uncountable and is measured in litres: 'How much oil? — a litre of oil.'

mcqs.q: ______ eggs? — A dozen eggs.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'How many'. Eggs are countable, and twelve eggs are called a dozen, which is the answer given in the shopping list.

mcqs.q: The beggar is asking for ______ money.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'some'. Money is uncountable, and for an indefinite amount the book uses 'some money' in Exercise 5.

mcqs.q: The teacher told the students to search for ______ information on Bhambore.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is '10 pages of'. Information is uncountable, so here it is measured in pages: the students had to search for 10 pages of information on Bhambore.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct question for rice?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'How much rice?' Rice is an uncountable noun, and uncountable nouns go with 'how much', as in the shopping list: 'How much rice? — a kilogram of rice.'

lessons.title: Writing: Paragraph Writing
lessons.notes_html:
How to Write a Paragraph

A good paragraph has one main idea. It begins with a topic sentence, and the other sentences give supporting details that develop the main idea.

Step 1: Brainstorm with a Mind Map

For the topic "Pollution", the class made a mind map with four branches:

  • Types: air pollution, water pollution, noise pollution, land pollution.
  • Causes: smoke from vehicles and factories, garbage heaps, loud horns, plastic waste.
  • Steps the government must take: make and enforce anti-pollution laws, arrange proper garbage collection, plant trees, punish those who pollute.
  • Steps citizens can take: throw garbage in bins, avoid unnecessary honking, plant trees, keep streets clean, spread awareness.

Step 2: Write on a Topic Sentence

  • "Pollution is all around us."
  • "There are many types of pollution."
  • "Pollution is caused by many things."
  • "The government should take steps to stop pollution."
  • "The citizens can do a number of things to stop pollution."

The same steps are then repeated for a new topic, "Playgrounds": first develop five topic sentences, then write a paragraph on one of them. For example, playgrounds give us many benefits — we play games there, become strong and healthy, learn teamwork and rules, and a fresh mind helps us study better.

mcqs.q: What is the first step the class takes before writing a paragraph on 'Pollution'?
options: Brainstorming and filling a mind map
mcqs.why: The correct answer is brainstorming and filling a mind map. In Writing Exercise 1, groups of five brainstorm on 'Pollution' and fill the mind map with four branches before any paragraph is written.

mcqs.q: A paragraph begins with ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a topic sentence. A topic sentence states the main idea of the paragraph, and the supporting details that follow develop that main idea.

mcqs.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four branches of the 'Pollution' mind map?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Famous buildings'. The four branches are: Types, Causes, Steps that the government must take, and Steps that citizens can take.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a type of pollution in the mind map?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is air pollution. The types branch lists air pollution, water pollution, noise pollution and land pollution.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a cause of pollution given in the lesson?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is smoke from vehicles and factories. The causes branch also includes garbage heaps, loud horns and plastic waste. Planting trees is a solution, not a cause.

mcqs.q: Which step must the government take, according to the mind map?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to make and enforce anti-pollution laws. The government branch also includes arranging proper garbage collection, planting trees and punishing those who pollute.

mcqs.q: Which step can citizens take to stop pollution?
options: Throw garbage in bins and keep streets clean
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to throw garbage in bins and keep streets clean. Citizens can also avoid unnecessary honking, plant trees and spread awareness, as the model paragraph in the book explains.

mcqs.q: What do supporting details do in a paragraph?
options: They develop the main idea of the topic sentence
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that they develop the main idea of the topic sentence. For example, the paragraph on 'There are many types of pollution' supports the topic sentence by describing air, water, noise and land pollution one by one.

mcqs.q: Which of these is one of the five topic sentences written on 'Pollution'?
options: 'The government should take steps to stop pollution.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'The government should take steps to stop pollution.' It is topic sentence 4 in Writing Exercise 2, and its paragraph describes laws, garbage collection, checking vehicle smoke and planting trees.

mcqs.q: According to the model paragraph, what is one benefit of playgrounds?
options: We learn to work in teams and follow rules
They make us tired and lazy
They are only for small children
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that we learn to work in teams and follow rules. The 'Playgrounds' paragraph also says playing keeps us strong and healthy and refreshes our minds so we can study better.

lessons.title: Study Skills: Free Writing
lessons.notes_html:
What Is Free Writing?

Free writing means writing without stopping for a short time every day. Its purpose is to overcome the fear of writing. You write freely and do not worry about mistakes.

The Steps of Free Writing

  • Spend just 5 minutes daily; keep a separate copy (notebook) for it.
  • Choose any topic — a person, place, thing, idea, TV programme, wedding, festival, or a fight with a brother, sister or friend.
  • Write without stopping, in any order.
  • Do not worry about punctuation, spelling, grammar or handwriting.
  • If you cannot think of an English word, write the word in another language and find the English word later.

A Sample Start

"Yesterday I went to my cousin's house. We played cricket in the street. The match was very interesting..." — notice how the writer simply keeps going without stopping to correct anything.

mcqs.q: For how long should we do free writing every day?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is five minutes. The first step of free writing in the book is: spend just 5 minutes daily, and keep a separate copy for it.

mcqs.q: What is the main purpose of free writing?
options: To prepare for a dictation test
To overcome the fear of writing
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to overcome the fear of writing. The unit's learning goals say: 'Doing free writing to overcome the fear of writing.' Because nothing is corrected, students stop being afraid of making mistakes.

mcqs.q: While free writing, we should write ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is without stopping. Step 3 of free writing says: write without stopping, in any order. Stopping to correct breaks the flow of ideas.

mcqs.q: What should we NOT worry about during free writing?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is punctuation, spelling, grammar and handwriting. The book clearly says not to worry about these while free writing; the aim is to get ideas onto paper freely.

mcqs.q: What should you do if you cannot think of an English word while free writing?
options: Write the word in another language and find the English word later
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to write the word in another language and find the English word later. This keeps the writing flowing instead of stopping at one difficult word.

mcqs.q: Where should free writing be done?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is in a separate copy. Step 1 of the book's free-writing instructions says to keep a separate copy for the daily five minutes of free writing.

mcqs.q: Which of these can be a free-writing topic?
options: A wedding, a festival, or a TV programme
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a wedding, a festival, or a TV programme. The book lists many possible topics: a person, place, thing, idea, TV programme, wedding, festival, or a fight with a brother, sister or friend.

mcqs.q: In free writing, in what order should we write our ideas?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is in any order. The book says 'Write without stopping, in any order' — the order does not matter because the aim is free expression, not a finished composition.

mcqs.q: The sample free writing in the book begins with a visit to ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a cousin's house. The sample start is: 'Yesterday I went to my cousin's house. We played cricket in the street. The match was very interesting...'

mcqs.q: Why does free writing help us become better writers?
options: It gives us marks in the exam
It removes the need to learn grammar forever
Regular practice without fear makes writing easier and more fluent
It teaches us to copy quickly
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that regular practice without fear makes writing easier and more fluent. Free writing is done daily for five minutes, and because mistakes are not corrected during it, students write more and lose their fear of writing.

lessons.title: Fun: Creativity — Controlling Pollution
lessons.notes_html:
The Fun Activity

In groups of three, pupils discuss and develop a mind map on what they can do to control pollution in four areas — the school, the playground, the neighbourhood and the roads. Then they develop a chart on one area and present it to the class.

Ideas from the Model Mind Map

  • School: put bins in every classroom, plant trees, stop burning garbage.
  • Playground: pick up litter after games, keep the ground clean.
  • Neighbourhood: hold a weekly cleanliness day, put up posters and handbills, ask shopkeepers to use bins.
  • Roads: request drivers not to honk without need, plant trees along roads.

The Sample Chart

The chart on "Our School, Pollution Free" shows drawings of bins, trees and clean classrooms with the message: "Keep our school clean — throw garbage in bins, plant trees, say no to pollution."

mcqs.q: In the Fun activity, pupils work in groups of ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is three. The book says: 'Work in groups of three. Discuss and develop a mind map on what you can do to control pollution...'

mcqs.q: The mind map in the Fun activity is about ______.
options: how to control pollution in different areas
mcqs.why: The correct answer is how to control pollution in different areas. The four areas are the school, the playground, the neighbourhood and the roads.

mcqs.q: Which area is NOT part of the Fun mind map?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the airport. The book names the school, the playground, the neighbourhood and the roads as the four areas for controlling pollution.

mcqs.q: What should be put in every classroom, according to the model mind map?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is bins. For the school, the model answer suggests putting bins in every classroom, planting trees and stopping the burning of garbage.

mcqs.q: What should pupils do in the playground after games?
options: Pick up litter and keep the ground clean
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to pick up litter and keep the ground clean. This is the playground branch of the model mind map in the Fun section.

mcqs.q: What is suggested for the neighbourhood in the mind map?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a weekly cleanliness day. The neighbourhood branch also includes posters and handbills and asking shopkeepers to use bins.

mcqs.q: What request is made to drivers in the 'Roads' branch?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is not to honk without need. Unnecessary honking causes noise pollution, and the mind map also suggests planting trees along the roads.

mcqs.q: After making the mind map, what do the groups develop and present?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a chart on one area. The book says: 'Then develop a chart on one area and present it.'

mcqs.q: What is the title of the sample chart in the model answer?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Our School, Pollution Free'. The chart shows drawings of bins, trees and clean classrooms with a message about keeping the school clean.

mcqs.q: What message is written on the sample chart?
options: 'Keep our school clean — throw garbage in bins, plant trees, say no to pollution.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the cleanliness message: 'Keep our school clean — throw garbage in bins, plant trees, say no to pollution.' It sums up the whole unit's theme in one line.

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: Problems and Solutions
lessons.notes_html:
About the Reading Text

Students could write any problem in the Students' Magazine. A person called Big Brother answered their letters. While signing their names, the students also wrote their feelings, to show how they felt. All five writers are students of secondary classes (VI–X).

The Five Students and Their Problems

  • Zain (Grade VI) — feeling unhappy. His grandparents tell his parents that he is an ill-mannered child, although he never talks to them harshly. Advice: greet them with a smile, help them carry their things, spend time with them, and be polite to them.
  • Ahsan (Grade IX) — feeling disturbed. Although he pays the full fare, the bus conductor always asks him to give up his seat for others, and his friends make fun of him. Advice: do not stop doing good things because friends mock you; feel honoured that God chose you to help (comfort) people.
  • Fahad (Class VII) — feeling penalized. Everyone points out his mistakes at lunch and dinner, so he has stopped eating with his family. Advice: he is lucky to have a caring family; practise mealtime manners — let elders and guests take food first, wait for your turn, eat with your mouth closed, with no burping and slurping.
  • Rashid (Class VII) — feeling annoyed. His friend Abid always argues with him and never listens first. Advice: respect other people's views and differences, because our society has a lot of diversity; for a lasting friendship, sometimes lose and let others win.
  • Sania (Class VI) — feeling frustrated. She has a dark complexion, the darkest among her siblings and friends, and feels inferior. Advice: physical appearance does not make a person better or more likeable; cleanliness and good behaviour are what matter — well-combed hair and clean clothes and shoes make everyone love you.

Word Meanings

  • upsets — makes unhappy
  • harsh — to say things in a rough manner
  • irritated — angry / annoyed
  • handicapped — having some disability
  • mock — make fun of
  • joint family — a family where husband, wife, children, parents and other family members live together
  • slurp — make a loud noise with the lips while eating or drinking
  • burp — make a noise while letting out air from the stomach through the mouth
  • diversity — variety
  • rituals — actions done at a fixed time in a fixed way
  • traditions — beliefs and practices passed down from elders
  • complexion — natural colour of the skin
  • fairer — lighter in colour
  • backbite — say bad things about people when they are not present

Good Manners — Remember

  • Always ask permission before entering someone's house or room.
  • Let elders and guests take the food first.
  • Use words like 'thank you', 'please', 'sorry' and 'excuse me' when needed.
  • Do not take more food than you can eat, do not grab someone's seat, and do not talk among yourselves during a speech.

mcqs.q: In which magazine could the students write their problems?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Students' Magazine. The summary in Exercise 7 begins: 'Students could write any problem in the Students' Magazine,' and a person called Big Brother gave them the answers.

mcqs.q: Who answered the students' problem letters?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Big Brother. The summary says: 'Someone called Big Brother gave them the answers.' The students added their feelings while writing their names, to show how they felt.

mcqs.q: The five students who shared their problems were students of ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is secondary classes (VI–X). Exercise 1 (A) gives this answer, and the five writers are in classes VI, IX, VII, VII and VI.

mcqs.q: Zain was feeling ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is unhappy. Zain's grandparents told his parents that he was an ill-mannered child, although he never talked to them harshly, so he felt unhappy.

mcqs.q: What was Zain advised to do for his grandparents?
options: Greet them with a smile, help them carry their things, spend time with them and be polite
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to greet them with a smile, help them carry their things, spend time with them, and be polite to them. This is the advice Big Brother gave Zain in the summary of Letter One.

mcqs.q: Why was Ahsan feeling disturbed?
options: The bus conductor always asked him to give up his seat, and his friends made fun of him
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that the bus conductor always asked him to give up his seat for others, although he paid the full fare, and his friends made fun of him whenever he was asked to stand up. These are the two main reasons in Exercise 6.

mcqs.q: What advice was Ahsan given?
options: Do not stop doing good things; feel honoured that God chose you to help people
mcqs.why: The correct answer is not to give up doing good things because his friends mocked him, but to feel honoured that God chose him to help (comfort/serve) people. Kindness is a good manner, even when others laugh.

mcqs.q: Fahad had stopped eating with his family because ______.
options: everyone pointed out his mistakes and scolded him at meal times
he did not like the food
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that everyone pointed out his mistakes at lunch and dinner and he was scolded at meal times, so he felt penalized and stopped sitting with his family.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a mealtime manner Fahad was asked to practise?
options: Allowing elders and guests to take food first
mcqs.why: The correct answer is allowing elders and guests to take food first. The advice also includes waiting for one's turn, eating in a proper manner with the mouth closed, and no burping and slurping.

mcqs.q: Rashid's problem was that his friend Abid ______.
options: always argued with him and did not listen to him first
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that Abid always argued with him, had a different point of view about everything, and did not listen to him first. That is why Rashid felt annoyed.

mcqs.q: For a lasting friendship, Rashid was advised to ______.
options: sometimes lose and let others win
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to sometimes lose and let others win. The advice also says to respect other people's views and differences because we live in a society that has a lot of diversity; then others will also lose sometimes and let him win.

mcqs.q: Why was Sania feeling frustrated?
options: She had lost her school bag
She had no friends at school
She had a dark complexion and felt inferior to people with fairer skin
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that she had a very dark complexion — the darkest among her siblings and friends — and whenever she saw people with fairer skin, she felt inferior.

mcqs.q: What did Big Brother tell Sania really matters in a person?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is cleanliness and good behaviour. Big Brother explained that physical appearances do not make a person better or more likeable; a person should have well-combed hair and clean clothes and shoes, and then everyone would love her.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'mock' mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to make fun of. In the vocabulary matching, 'mock' is paired with 'make fun of' — Ahsan's friends mocked him when the conductor asked him to give up his seat.

mcqs.q: Which of these is good manners?
options: Using words like 'thank you', 'please', 'sorry' and 'excuse me' when needed
Taking a lot of food, more than you can eat
Quickly taking the seat of someone who left to get something
Talking among yourselves during a speech
mcqs.why: The correct answer is using polite words like 'thank you', 'please', 'sorry' and 'excuse me' when needed. In the pre-reading bubbles activity, this statement gets a smiling face (good manners), while the other three get sad faces (bad manners).

lessons.title: Speaking: Reasons for Opinions and Actions
lessons.notes_html:
What We Practise

In section 2.2 we practise giving reasons for opinions and actions. Zeba, Najma and Jena talk together and explain why they want to do something.

The Model Dialogue — Key Ideas

  • Zeba suggests: "Let us go and ask mother now."
  • Najma agrees and gives a reason: "Yes, and we will promise to study again after our bath."
  • Jena adds another good reason: "Then we can play in the evening with fresh minds, because we have already studied for three hours."

How to Give Reasons

  • Use because to join your opinion or action with its reason: "We can play in the evening because we have already studied for three hours."
  • First state what you think or want to do, then support it with a sensible reason.
  • After practising the given dialogue in groups of three, think of one more dialogue of your own and write it in the given space.

mcqs.q: What speaking skill is practised in section 2.2?
options: Giving reasons for opinions and actions
mcqs.why: The correct answer is giving reasons for opinions and actions. The section title is 'Speaking: Reasons for opinions and actions', and the dialogue of Zeba, Najma and Jena is built on supporting ideas with reasons.

mcqs.q: The dialogue in section 2.2 is between ______.
options: The class and the head teacher
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Zeba, Najma and Jena. The exercise says: 'Work in groups of three and practise the dialogue between Zeba, Najma and Jena about giving reasons for opinions and actions.'

mcqs.q: In how many members is the dialogue practised?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is groups of three. There are three speakers — Zeba, Najma and Jena — so pupils practise in groups of three and take one role each.

mcqs.q: What does Najma promise so that they can ask mother?
options: To study again after their bath
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to study again after their bath. In the model dialogue Najma says: 'Yes, and we will promise to study again after our bath.'

mcqs.q: Why can the girls play in the evening with fresh minds?
options: Because they have already studied for three hours
Because they have slept all day
Because mother told them to play
mcqs.why: The correct answer is because they have already studied for three hours. Jena gives this reason in the dialogue: after studying for three hours, playing in the evening will refresh their minds.

mcqs.q: Which word joins an action with its reason in the dialogue?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'because'. Jena says: '...then we can play in the evening with fresh minds, because we have already studied for three hours.' 'Because' introduces the reason.

mcqs.q: What does Zeba suggest at the start of the dialogue?
options: 'Let us go and ask mother now.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Let us go and ask mother now.' The model dialogue opens with Zeba's suggestion, and the others support it with reasons.

mcqs.q: A good reason for an opinion should be ______.
options: sensible and connected to the opinion
mcqs.why: The correct answer is sensible and connected to the opinion. In the dialogue, each girl supports her idea with a reason that truly fits it — for example, studying after the bath and having already studied for three hours.

mcqs.q: After practising the given dialogue, what else must the groups do?
options: Memorise the dialogue word by word
Think of one more dialogue of their own and write it in the given space
Act it for another class only
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to think of one more dialogue of their own and write it in the given space. The exercise asks pupils first to practise Zeba, Najma and Jena's dialogue and then to create their own on the same pattern.

mcqs.q: Which sentence gives a reason correctly?
options: We should rest because we are tired.
We should rest because the sky is blue.
We should rest because bananas are yellow.
We should rest because two and two make four.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'We should rest because we are tired.' The reason must explain the action; like the dialogue's reasons, being tired is a sensible reason for resting, while the other 'reasons' have no connection with the action.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Articles — A and An
lessons.notes_html:
The Rule for 'a' and 'an'

We use a or an only before a single countable noun.

  • Use a before a consonant sound: a room, a kite, a finger.
  • Use an before a vowel sound: an apple, an orange, an hour (the 'h' in 'hour' is silent, so it begins with a vowel sound).
  • Use no article before uncountable nouns: food, water, milk (we say "some food", "some water").
  • Use no article before plural nouns: tables, vans, eyes (we say "some tables" or "two tables").

Adjectives with Nouns (Exercise 2)

  • tasty food (no article — uncountable)
  • an untidy room, a sweet apple, a fast kite
  • dirty water, creamy milk (no article — uncountable)
  • twenty tables, black vans, oval eyes (no article — plural)
  • an unripe orange, an early hour, an injured finger

Using Them in Sentences (Exercise 3)

  • Mansoor bought a fast kite for the kite flying competition.
  • My mother made pudding with creamy milk.
  • Drinking dirty water can make us fall sick.
  • The baby has brown hair and oval eyes.
  • I like eating a sweet apple every day.

mcqs.q: Which is correct? ______ room.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'a'. 'Room' is a single countable noun beginning with a consonant sound, so we say 'a room'.

mcqs.q: Which is correct? ______ apple.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'an'. 'Apple' is a single countable noun beginning with a vowel sound, so we use 'an apple'.

mcqs.q: Which is correct? ______ water (as a noun by itself).
mcqs.why: The correct answer is no article. Water is uncountable, so we do not put 'a' or 'an' before it; we say 'some water', just as the book's answer explains.

mcqs.q: Which is correct? ______ hour.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'an'. The 'h' in 'hour' is silent, so 'hour' begins with a vowel sound, and we say 'an hour' and 'an early hour'.

mcqs.q: Which is correct? ______ tables.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is no article. 'Tables' is countable but plural, and 'a/an' is used only for single nouns; we say 'some tables' or 'twenty tables'.

mcqs.q: Which is correct? ______ orange.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'an'. 'Orange' begins with a vowel sound, so we say 'an orange' and 'an unripe orange'.

mcqs.q: Which is correct? ______ milk.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is no article. Milk is uncountable; in Exercise 2 the book pairs it with an adjective but no article: 'creamy milk'.

mcqs.q: Which is correct? ______ finger.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'a'. 'Finger' is a single countable noun beginning with a consonant sound, so the noun alone takes 'a finger'. (In Exercise 2 the pair is 'an injured finger' because the adjective 'injured', which comes first, begins with a vowel sound.)

mcqs.q: Mansoor bought ______ for the kite flying competition.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'a fast kite'. In Exercise 3 the adjective-noun pair from Exercise 2 completes the sentence, with the article 'a' because 'kite' is single and countable and 'fast' begins with a consonant sound.

mcqs.q: My mother made pudding with ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'creamy milk'. Milk is uncountable, so no 'a' or 'an' is used even when an adjective comes before it.

mcqs.q: Drinking ______ can make us fall sick.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'dirty water'. Water is uncountable, so the adjective-noun pair is used without an article, exactly as in Exercise 3.

mcqs.q: Get up at ______ and you will be able to complete all your work.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'an early hour'. 'Early' begins with a vowel sound, and 'hour' itself has a silent 'h', so 'an' is used in both cases.

mcqs.q: The baby has brown hair and ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'oval eyes'. 'Eyes' is plural, and 'a/an' cannot be used with plural nouns, so the pair stands without an article.

mcqs.q: Please don't buy ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'an unripe orange'. The adjective 'unripe' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an' is used before the single countable noun phrase.

mcqs.q: The people were afraid because the ______ were racing against each other.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'black vans'. 'Vans' is plural, so no 'a' or 'an' is used; this is the completed sentence from Exercise 3 of the book.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Reflexive Pronouns
lessons.notes_html:
What Are Reflexive Pronouns?

Reflexive pronouns end in -self (singular) or -selves (plural). We use them when the doer and the receiver of the action are the same person, or after 'by' to mean 'alone / without help'.

  • I — myself: I hurt myself while cleaning the kitchen.
  • you — yourself / yourselves: You told yourself that you bought it. / All of you will have to go yourselves.
  • he — himself: He danced by himself on the stage.
  • she — herself: She photographed herself.
  • it — itself: The horse hurt itself. / The car started moving by itself.
  • we — ourselves: We changed ourselves.
  • they — themselves: They trained themselves for the match.

Examples from the Exercises

  • Raza ended up fixing it by himself one afternoon.
  • We must avoid reporting things that we haven't seen ourselves.
  • My brother and I served snacks to the guests ourselves as our mother was not home.
  • We should not fight amongst ourselves.
  • Matching answers: "Who did your homework?" — "I did myself." "Did the mechanic repair their car?" — "No, they repaired themselves."

Note on the Book

Exercise 5 asks us to use each pronoun only once, but as the book's own notes show, 'herself' and 'myself' are needed more than once — the rule cannot be fully satisfied as printed. The book also prints "which cleaning" (for "while cleaning") and "Irellised" (for "I realised") — these are typos.

mcqs.q: I hurt ______ while cleaning the kitchen.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'myself'. The subject is 'I', and the person who acts and the person who is hurt are the same, so the reflexive pronoun is 'myself'.

mcqs.q: She photographed ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'herself'. For the subject 'she', the reflexive pronoun is 'herself' — she took her own photograph.

mcqs.q: They trained ______ for the match.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'themselves'. The subject 'they' is plural, and plural reflexive pronouns end in '-selves': themselves, ourselves, yourselves.

mcqs.q: He danced ______ on the stage. (alone)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'by himself'. 'By + reflexive pronoun' means alone or without help; for 'he' we use 'himself'.

mcqs.q: We changed ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'ourselves'. The subject is 'we', so the reflexive pronoun is 'ourselves'.

mcqs.q: The horse hurt ______ while trying to escape.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'itself'. For animals and things ('it'), the reflexive pronoun is 'itself' — the same form used for the car that 'started moving by itself'.

mcqs.q: Raza ended up fixing it ______ one afternoon. (without help)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'by himself'. Raza is male and he fixed it alone, so the book's answer is 'fixing it by himself one afternoon'.

mcqs.q: We must avoid reporting things that we haven't seen ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'ourselves'. The subject is 'we', so the reflexive pronoun that matches is 'ourselves'.

mcqs.q: My brother and I served snacks to the guests ______ as our mother was not home.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'ourselves'. 'My brother and I' means 'we', and serving without mother's help is expressed with 'ourselves'.

mcqs.q: 'Who did your homework?' — Choose the matching answer from Exercise 6.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'I did myself.' In the matching exercise, question 1 'Who did your homework?' is paired with answer (f) 'I did myself' — this pair is given as the example in the book.

lessons.title: Writing: Short Informal Letters
lessons.notes_html:
Short Informal Letters

An informal letter is written to friends and family. It is friendly in tone, begins with "Dear ___," and often ends with "Yours sincerely," followed by the writer's name.

The Letters in This Unit

  • Geeta's reply to Marvi: Marvi's sister is ill with typhoid and must rest for two weeks, so Geeta tells her what work was done in class (two lessons from Unit 2, homework of Exercises 3 and 4, and the English dialogue practice) and offers to lend her notebook.
  • Jawed's letter to Nadeem: Jawed asks to borrow a book on General History because his brother is working on a project about the Industrial Revolution in Europe.
  • A borrowing letter: the writer asks to borrow a science notebook and a geometry box for two days, explains why (he was absent when the teacher explained the diagrams), and says when he will return them (on Friday).
  • The response: the friend agrees, asks him to take care of the things, and reminds him to return them by Friday for his own revision.

What a Borrowing Letter Must Mention

  • What you want to borrow.
  • Why you want it.
  • When you will return it.

mcqs.q: Why did Marvi write to Geeta?
options: To invite her to a party
To ask what work was done in class, because her sister was ill
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to ask what work was done in class because her sister was ill. Marvi's sister is ill with typhoid and must rest for two weeks, so she needs to know the class work.

mcqs.q: What illness does Marvi's sister have?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is typhoid. The book says Marvi's sister 'is ill with typhoid and must rest for two weeks'.

mcqs.q: What does Geeta offer to lend Marvi's sister?
options: Her notebook, so she can copy the work
mcqs.why: The correct answer is her notebook. Geeta writes that she will lend her notebook so that Marvi's sister can copy the class work when she feels better.

mcqs.q: Why does Jawed want a book on General History?
options: His brother is working on a project about the Industrial Revolution in Europe
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that his brother is working on a project about the Industrial Revolution in Europe. Jawed's letter to Nadeem — the letter to which Nadeem's reply was written — explains this need.

mcqs.q: Where did Nadeem see a good book on General History?
options: At a second-hand bookshop in Saddar
mcqs.why: The correct answer is at a second-hand bookshop in Saddar. Nadeem did not have the book himself, but he had seen a good one there, as the unit's second writing exercise explains.

mcqs.q: In the model borrowing letter, what two things does the writer ask to borrow?
options: A science notebook and a geometry box
A story book and a pen
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a science notebook and a geometry box. The writer needs them for two days to complete his notes before the test.

mcqs.q: Why does the writer need to borrow the notebook and geometry box?
options: He was absent when the teacher explained the diagrams
He lost his own in the bus
His friend asked him to get them
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that he was absent when the teacher explained the diagrams. A good borrowing letter always gives a clear reason, as this model letter does.

mcqs.q: When will the writer return the borrowed things?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is on Friday. Both the borrowing letter and the reply mention Friday — the writer promises to return them then, and the friend needs them back for his own revision.

mcqs.q: How does an informal letter usually begin and end?
options: 'Dear ___,' and 'Yours sincerely,' with the writer's name
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Dear ___,' at the start and 'Yours sincerely,' with the name at the end. All the model letters in this unit — Geeta's, Jawed's, Ahmed's and Ali's — follow this informal pattern.

mcqs.q: Which three things must a letter asking to borrow something mention?
options: The price, the shop and the date
The weather, the news and a joke
Your class, your roll number and your marks
What you want, why you want it, and when you will return it
mcqs.why: The correct answer is what you want, why you want it, and when you will return it. The book's Exercise 2 states these three points, and the model letter includes all of them.

lessons.title: Study Skills: Cloze Passage
lessons.notes_html:
Self-Created Cloze

A cloze passage is a paragraph with some words removed. In a self-created cloze, you make the passage yourself and then fill the blanks from memory.

Step 1: Make and Fill the Cloze

  • Choose a paragraph from the Reading Comprehension section (or any English book).
  • Mark or underline every 8th word.
  • Open your notebook, draw a margin, and put the date.
  • Copy the paragraph in your best handwriting, leaving a blank line where each marked word was.
  • Close the books, take a break of half an hour, then fill in the blanks without looking at the original.

Step 2: Check Your Work

  • Check: margin drawn, date written, paragraph started two-finger space from the margin, writing neat and tidy.
  • Open the textbook, check the answers, and give yourself one mark for each correct answer.

Remember

Also keep doing your free writing every day (Unit 1), following the same steps: choose any topic, write without stopping for 5 minutes, and do not worry about spelling or grammar.

mcqs.q: In a self-created cloze, which word is marked in the paragraph?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is every 8th word. Step 1 of the self-created cloze says: choose a paragraph and 'mark or underline every 8th word'.

mcqs.q: From where should the paragraph for the cloze be chosen?
options: From the Reading Comprehension section or any English book
mcqs.why: The correct answer is from the Reading Comprehension section (or any English book). The book allows either source for the self-created cloze paragraph.

mcqs.q: What should be written at the top before copying the paragraph?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a margin and the date. Step 1 says: 'Open your notebook, draw a margin, and put the date,' and Step 2 checks that both were done.

mcqs.q: How should the paragraph be copied into the notebook?
options: In your best handwriting, leaving a blank where each marked word was
mcqs.why: The correct answer is in your best handwriting, leaving a blank line where each marked word was. Those blanks are what you will later fill from memory.

mcqs.q: How long a break should you take before filling the blanks?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is half an hour. The book says: 'Close the books, take a break of half an hour, then fill in the blanks without looking at the original.'

mcqs.q: While filling the blanks, you should ______.
options: fill them without looking at the original
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to fill them without looking at the original. The break and the closed book make it a real test of memory and understanding.

mcqs.q: How many marks do you give yourself for each correct answer?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is one mark. Step 2 (check) says: 'give yourself one mark for each correct answer' after comparing with the textbook.

mcqs.q: The paragraph should be started ______ from the margin.
options: in the middle of the page
mcqs.why: The correct answer is two-finger space. This is one of the checking points in Step 2, along with the margin, the date and neat, tidy writing.

mcqs.q: What is checked in Step 2 besides the answers?
options: Margin drawn, date written, neat and tidy writing
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the margin, the date and neat, tidy writing. Step 2 is a self-check of both presentation and the correctness of the filled words.

mcqs.q: The Study Skills section also reminds us to ______ every day.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to do free writing every day. Exercise 2 of Study Skills says: 'Remember to do your free writing every day,' following the five-minute steps learnt in Unit 1.

lessons.title: Fun: Creativity — Funny One-Line Solutions
lessons.notes_html:
Be a Big Brother / Big Sister

Imagine you are the Big Brother or Big Sister of a students' magazine, like the one in the reading lesson. This time, give a funny one-line solution to each small problem.

The Book's Example

  • Problem: "My homework is always incomplete because I like to watch television."
  • Funny solution: "Look at the television while doing your homework — but it should be off." (This one is given as the example in the book.)

More Funny Solutions from the Exercise

  • "I wake up late and have to miss my breakfast." — "Eat your breakfast in your dreams — or keep a sandwich under your pillow!"
  • "My parents tell me that I am lazy although I always do all my work on time." — "Do your work so fast that your parents think you are still sleeping!"
  • "My friends are jealous of me because I get good marks." — "Share your marks with them — give everyone ten marks from your total!"
  • "I don't like outdoor games and my friends don't like indoor games." — "Play indoor games outdoors — put the carrom board in the playground!"
  • "I study very hard but I always get very low marks." — "Study the teacher's mind instead of the book — then you will guess the questions!"
  • "I am a very quiet and shy person, so I don't have any friends." — "Make friends with your shadow — it never leaves you and never argues!"
  • "My friends tease me a lot because I often fall asleep in class." — "Sleep with your eyes open — then your friends will think you are studying hard!"
  • "I always forget my homework at home." — "Keep your homework in your shoes — you never forget to wear those!"
  • "I am afraid of examinations." — "Invite the examination to tea — once it becomes your friend, it will not frighten you!"

mcqs.q: In the Fun activity, you imagine yourself as ______ of a students' magazine.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Big Brother / Big Sister. The Fun section says: 'Imagine you are Big Brother/Big Sister of a students' magazine,' like the person who answered letters in the reading text.

mcqs.q: What kind of solution must you give to each problem?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a funny one-line solution. Each problem in the Fun exercise is answered with one short, humorous line.

mcqs.q: Which problem-and-solution pair is given as the example in the book?
options: Late waking — keep a sandwich under the pillow
Fear of examinations — invite it to tea
Watching television and incomplete homework — look at the TV while doing homework, but it should be off
Forgetting homework — keep it in your shoes
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the television one. The book marks 'Look at the television while doing your homework — but it should be off' as the given example solution.

mcqs.q: What is the funny solution for 'I wake up late and have to miss my breakfast'?
options: Eat your breakfast in your dreams — or keep a sandwich under your pillow
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Eat your breakfast in your dreams — or keep a sandwich under your pillow!' It is a model funny solution from the Fun exercise.

mcqs.q: What is the funny solution for a shy person who has no friends?
options: Make friends with your shadow — it never leaves you and never argues
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Make friends with your shadow — it never leaves you and never argues!' This is the model solution for the problem 'I am a very quiet and shy person, so I don't have any friends.'

mcqs.q: What is the funny solution for 'My friends tease me because I often fall asleep in class'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Sleep with your eyes open — then your friends will think you are studying hard!' It is one of the model one-line solutions in the Fun section.

mcqs.q: What is the funny solution for friends who are jealous of good marks?
options: Share your marks — give everyone ten marks from your total
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Share your marks with them — give everyone ten marks from your total!' The humour comes from treating marks like sweets that can be shared.

mcqs.q: What is the funny solution when you like indoor games but your friends like outdoor games (or the reverse)?
options: Play indoor games outdoors — put the carrom board in the playground
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Play indoor games outdoors — put the carrom board in the playground!' It solves the difference in a funny, friendly way.

mcqs.q: What is the funny solution for 'I always forget my homework at home'?
options: Keep your homework in your shoes — you never forget to wear those
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Keep your homework in your shoes — you never forget to wear those!' This is one of the two problems pupils add with their own funny solutions (model answer in the book).

mcqs.q: What is the funny solution for 'I am afraid of examinations'?
options: Invite the examination to tea — once it becomes your friend, it will not frighten you
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Invite the examination to tea — once it becomes your friend, it will not frighten you!' Like all the Fun solutions, it turns a worry into a joke in one line.

chapters.title: Awareness of Crisis, Accidents and Natural Calamities

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: Learning to Live in a Critical Situation
lessons.notes_html:
The Story in Short — Zubair and the Flood

When it rains a lot in the monsoon season, rivers overflow and floods can destroy homes, crops and roads. People lose their homes, food and belongings; drinking water becomes dirty and diseases spread. This story is about a boy named Zubair. Zubair did not drown in the flood because he had clung to a log and floated on it the whole night, so at the beginning of the story he was very tired. Sadly, his mother was washed away by the fast flowing water — she drowned. Soldiers came in a boat and took him to a relief camp, where there were hundreds of people and the flood victims were given food, shelter and medicines.

At the camp Zubair was upset to see people suffering, and every time he closed his eyes he saw the scene of his mother being washed away. He wanted to do something so that people would not suffer every year — he did not want other children to become orphans. With a volunteer's help he developed a programme: they gathered people and told them what to do before, during and after a flood. They wrote the points on a large white bedsheet because they did not have large sheets of paper. That night Zubair did not see his mother drowning; instead he dreamt that his mother was happy and praised him. He woke up fresh and energetic.

Word Meanings

  • unharmed — not hurt in any way
  • gushing — moving with great force
  • clung — held on (to something)
  • bumping — hitting
  • numb — without feeling
  • exhausted — very, very tired
  • yelled — shouted
  • relief camp — a place where people who have lost their homes get food and shelter
  • evacuate — leave a place when there is danger
  • nightmare — a bad and frightening dream
  • glittered — shone
  • energetic — active

Flood Safety — Before, During and After

  • Before: pack a bag with important items; listen to the radio and television for flood information; if the government tells people to leave their houses, they must do so immediately.
  • During: carry only the most important items while leaving home; do not touch electric wires while standing in water; do not walk through flowing water.
  • After: wash and clean the objects covered with mud; stay away from fallen power lines; return home only when told it is safe.

Why the Safety Steps Matter

  • Use a stick to check the ground while walking in flood water — this can protect you from falling in a ditch.
  • Young people should hold the hands of older people and children — they may flow away with the water.
  • Carry only the most important things — it is difficult to walk with a heavy load.
  • Keep away from fallen electric poles or wires — they can be harmful due to the electric current flowing through them.
  • Avoid bathing and walking in flood water — it can be dirty and have harmful things that make people fall sick.

mcqs.q: The story in Unit 3 is about a ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a flood. Exercise 1 asks exactly this question, and the whole story — Zubair clinging to a log, the relief camp and the safety points — is about a flood.

mcqs.q: Zubair was saved by ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is soldiers. In the story sequence, soldiers came in a boat and took Zubair to a relief camp.

mcqs.q: How many people were there in the relief camp?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is hundreds of people. Exercise 1 gives this answer; at the camp the flood victims were given food, shelter and medicines.

mcqs.q: Why did Zubair not drown in the flood?
options: He had clung to a log
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that he had clung to a log. Exercise 5 matches the statement 'Zubair did not drown because...' with the reason 'he had clung to a log', and he floated on it the whole night.

mcqs.q: Why did tears come out of Zubair's eyes?
options: He was happy to be safe
His mother had drowned in the flood water
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that his mother had drowned in the flood water. Exercise 5 gives this reason, and in the story Zubair repeatedly saw the scene of his mother being washed away by the fast flowing water.

mcqs.q: What did Zubair decide to do in the relief camp?
options: Go back to his village at once
Tell people how to protect themselves during flood times
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to tell people how to protect themselves during flood times. Exercise 3 gives this answer; Zubair wanted to do something so that people would not suffer every year.

mcqs.q: Why did Zubair want to help others?
options: He did not want other children to become orphans
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that he did not want other children to become orphans. Exercise 5 matches 'Zubair wanted to do something because...' with this reason — he had lost his own mother and wished to save others from the same pain.

mcqs.q: Why was Zubair upset at the relief camp?
options: He did not like seeing people suffer so much
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that he did not like seeing people suffer so much. This is the reason matched in Exercise 5, and it pushed him to develop the safety programme with a volunteer.

mcqs.q: At the end of the story, why was Zubair fresh and energetic?
options: He had given a good presentation
His mother came in his dream and liked what he had done
He had slept for two days
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that his mother came in his dream and liked what he had done. Exercise 3 gives this answer: instead of the nightmare of his mother drowning, he dreamt she was happy and praised him.

mcqs.q: What does 'relief camp' mean?
options: A place where people who have lost their homes get food and shelter
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a place where people who have lost their homes get food and shelter. This is the meaning given in the vocabulary matching of Exercise 2.

mcqs.q: What does 'evacuate' mean?
options: To leave a place when there is danger
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to leave a place when there is danger. During floods, if the government tells people to evacuate, they should do so immediately because their houses may be devastated by the flood.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a 'Before the flood' safety step?
options: Stay away from fallen power lines
Return home when told it is safe
Pack a bag with important items
mcqs.why: The correct answer is packing a bag with important items. In Exercise 4, packing a bag and listening to radio/TV for information are 'Before' steps; washing mud-covered objects and returning home are 'After' steps.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a 'During the flood' safety step?
options: Listen to flood information on TV
Pack a bag with important items
Do not touch electric wires while standing in water
mcqs.why: The correct answer is not touching electric wires while standing in water. Carrying only important items and not walking through flowing water are also 'During' steps in Exercise 4.

mcqs.q: Why should people use a stick to check the ground while walking in flood water?
options: It can protect them from falling in a ditch
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that it can protect them from falling in a ditch. Exercise 7 matches this statement with this reason from the box.

mcqs.q: Why should people avoid bathing and walking in flood water?
options: It can be dirty and have harmful things that can make them fall sick
The water is too deep everywhere
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that flood water can be dirty and have harmful things that can make people fall sick. This is the correct reason chosen from the box in Exercise 7.

lessons.title: Speaking: Expressing Ability and Inability
lessons.notes_html:
What We Practise

In section 3.2, pupils interview each other in groups of three with can / can't questions and give reasons for expressing ability and inability to do something.

The Three Interview Cards

  • Card 1: "Can you play table tennis?"
  • Card 2: "Can you cook anything?"
  • Card 3: "Can you speak Arabic?"

Each classmate gives one positive answer with a reason and one negative answer with a reason:

  • "Yes, I can play table tennis because I practise every day." / "No, I can't play table tennis because I never learnt it."
  • "Yes, I can cook rice because my mother taught me." / "No, I can't cook anything because I never tried."
  • "Yes, I can speak Arabic because I learn it at school." / "No, I can't speak Arabic because it is difficult for me."

Reporting Back to the Class

Then pupils come up one by one and tell the class what their partner can or cannot do — one positive and one negative sentence. Example: "Ali can play table tennis because he practises every day. Sara can't cook anything because she never tried."

mcqs.q: In the speaking activity, pupils work in groups of ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is three. The book says: 'In groups of three, interview each other with can/can't questions and give reasons.'

mcqs.q: What kind of questions are asked in the interview?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is questions with 'can' and 'can't' about ability. The three cards ask: 'Can you play table tennis?', 'Can you cook anything?' and 'Can you speak Arabic?'

mcqs.q: What must each answer include besides 'can' or 'can't'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a reason. The section practises giving reasons for expressing ability and inability: 'Yes, I can... because...' and 'No, I can't... because...'

mcqs.q: Which is a correct positive answer from the model?
options: Yes, I can play table tennis because I never learnt it.
Yes, I can play table tennis because I practise every day.
Yes, I can cook rice because nobody taught me.
Yes, I can speak Arabic because it is difficult.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Yes, I can play table tennis because I practise every day.' The reason must support the ability; the other options give reasons that contradict the 'can'.

mcqs.q: Which is a correct negative answer from the model?
options: No, I can't play table tennis because I practise daily.
No, I can't cook because I cook every day.
No, I can't speak Arabic because it is difficult for me.
No, I can't cook anything because my mother taught me.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'No, I can't speak Arabic because it is difficult for me.' A 'can't' answer needs a reason that explains the inability, like never learning or finding something difficult.

mcqs.q: Why can the pupil cook rice, according to Card 2's model answer?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is because his mother taught him. The model answer for Card 2 is: 'Yes, I can cook rice because my mother taught me.'

mcqs.q: After the interviews, what do pupils do one by one?
options: Tell the class what their partner can do or cannot do
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to tell the class what their partner can do or cannot do. The report-back asks for one positive and one negative sentence about the partner.

mcqs.q: Which is a correct report-back sentence?
options: Ali cans play table tennis everyday because.
Ali can play table tennis because never.
Ali play table tennis can because practises.
Ali can play table tennis because he practises every day.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Ali can play table tennis because he practises every day.' It is the model report sentence in the book, with 'can' before the verb and 'because' introducing the reason.

mcqs.q: How many answers does each classmate give in the interview?
options: One positive answer with a reason and one negative answer with a reason
mcqs.why: The correct answer is one positive answer with a reason and one negative answer with a reason. This is what the speaking exercise instructs for each of the three cards.

mcqs.q: Which question belongs to the interview cards?
options: Can you swim in the sea?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Can you speak Arabic?' The three cards ask about playing table tennis, cooking anything, and speaking Arabic.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Conditional Sentences — First Conditional
lessons.notes_html:
The First Conditional

We use the first conditional to talk about a possible action and its likely result:

If + present simple, ... will + verb — "If you work hard, you will get good grades."

Matching Examples (Exercise 1)

  • If it rains, I will stay at home.
  • If father allows me, I will go with you.
  • If he helps Abdul, he will not have any problem.
  • If Amma makes the halwa, we will enjoy eating it.
  • If Salma sings well, she will win the singing competition.
  • If I feed the dog, it will take care of my house.
  • If she treats the children nicely, they will always listen to her.

Punctuation Rules

  • When the if-clause comes first, put a comma after it: "If Alina works fast, she will finish her work on time."
  • When the if-clause comes at the end, no comma is used: "Alina will finish her work on time if she works fast."

The Chain Story

The pattern can be chained, where each result becomes the next condition: "If he goes home on foot, he will not reach home on time. If he doesn't reach home on time, his parents will get worried. If his parents get worried, they will telephone the school..."

mcqs.q: Which sentence is a correct first conditional?
options: If you worked hard yesterday tomorrow.
If you work hard, you will get good grades.
If hard work, grades you will.
If you will work hard, you get grades good.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'If you work hard, you will get good grades.' The first conditional pattern is: If + present simple, will + verb — and a comma is used when the if-clause comes first.

mcqs.q: If it rains, ______.
options: I stayed at home yesterday morning
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'I will stay at home'. This is the matching pair from Exercise 1: the if-clause about rain joins the result about staying at home.

mcqs.q: If father allows me, ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'I will go with you'. In the first conditional, the result clause uses 'will + base verb', as in this matching pair from Exercise 1.

mcqs.q: When the if-clause comes first, we put ______ after it.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a comma. Exercise 2 reminds us: 'use a comma after the if clause' — for example, 'If Alina works fast, she will finish her work on time.'

mcqs.q: Which sentence is written correctly with the if-clause at the end?
options: Alina will finish her work on time if she works fast.
Alina will finish her work on time, if she works fast.
Alina will finish her work on time if, she works fast.
Alina will finish, her work on time if she works fast.
