mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Alina will finish her work on time if she works fast.' Exercise 3 explains that when the if-clause is moved to the end, no comma is used.

mcqs.q: If Salma sings well, ______.
options: she won the competition last year only
she will win the singing competition
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'she will win the singing competition'. This is the correct match from Exercise 1, following the first-conditional pattern.

mcqs.q: If I feed the dog, ______.
options: it will take care of my house
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'it will take care of my house'. This completes the first-conditional pair from Exercise 1 with 'will + verb' in the result clause.

mcqs.q: Complete the model sentence: 'If the weather becomes sunny, ______.'
options: we will play in the park
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'we will play in the park'. This is the book's model completion in Exercise 2, using will + verb for the likely result.

mcqs.q: In the chain story, if the boy doesn't reach home on time, ______.
options: his parents got worried yesterday morning at five
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'his parents will get worried'. The chain story continues the pattern: each result becomes the next 'if' — 'If his parents get worried, they will telephone the school.'

mcqs.q: Which part is the if-clause in 'If we help others, they will help us too'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'If we help others'. The if-clause gives the condition (present simple), and 'they will help us too' is the result clause with 'will'.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Joining Sentences with And and But
lessons.notes_html:
Joining Sentences with 'and' and 'but'

  • Use and to join two similar or adding ideas: "This flower is very beautiful and it smells nice too."
  • Use but to join two opposite or contrasting ideas: "Salma loves mangoes but she does not like oranges."

Examples from the Exercises

  • The white cup is full but the blue one is empty.
  • We are on time but the train is late.
  • My brother plays cricket and hockey.
  • I like climbing trees and jumping from trees.
  • Their house is far from the school but our house is near the school.
  • I am short but my brother is very tall.
  • My mobile phone fell down but it did not break.
  • Ram Chand bowled well but he did not get a wicket.
  • Razia washed her clothes and cleaned her room.
  • Karim and James worked hard and they both got good grades.

Asking and Joining (Exercise 8)

Partners ask each other paired questions (When do you get up? / When do you go to bed? Do you like animals? / birds? Have you climbed a mountain? / a tree? ...) and then join each pair of answers with 'but' or 'and': "My friend gets up at 6 o'clock in the morning but goes to bed at 10 o'clock at night." "He has never climbed a mountain but he has climbed a tree."

mcqs.q: Salma loves mangoes. She does not like oranges. Join the sentences.
options: Salma loves mangoes and she does not like oranges.
Salma loves mangoes so she does not like oranges because.
Salma loves mangoes but she does not like oranges.
Salma loves mangoes, oranges she does not like but and.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Salma loves mangoes but she does not like oranges.' The two ideas are opposite — loving one fruit and not liking another — so they are joined with 'but'.

mcqs.q: This flower is very beautiful. It smells nice too. Join the sentences.
options: This flower is very beautiful or it smells nice too.
This flower beautiful smells and too nice is.
This flower is very beautiful but it smells nice too.
This flower is very beautiful and it smells nice too.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'This flower is very beautiful and it smells nice too.' Both ideas are positive and add to each other, so they are joined with 'and'.

mcqs.q: The white cup is full. The blue one is empty. Join the sentences.
options: The white cup is full and the blue one is full too.
The white cup is full but the blue one is empty.
The white cup is full because the blue one is empty and.
The white cup is full and the blue one is empty full.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'The white cup is full but the blue one is empty.' Full and empty are opposites, so the joining word is 'but'.

mcqs.q: We are on time. The train is late. Join the sentences.
options: We are on time and the train is late too both same.
We are on time, the train is late and we are late.
We are on time or the train is late always.
We are on time but the train is late.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'We are on time but the train is late.' Our being on time and the train's being late are contrasting ideas, so 'but' is correct.

mcqs.q: My brother plays cricket. My brother plays hockey. Join the sentences.
options: My brother plays cricket, hockey but.
My brother plays cricket but hockey.
My brother plays cricket or hockey never.
My brother plays cricket and hockey.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'My brother plays cricket and hockey.' The two games are similar, adding ideas, so they join with 'and' — and the repeated words can be dropped.

mcqs.q: My mobile phone fell down. It did not break. Join the sentences.
options: My mobile phone fell down but it did not break.
My mobile phone fell down, but it broke not and.
My mobile phone fell down and it broke.
My mobile phone fell down and it did not break same.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'My mobile phone fell down but it did not break.' Falling down suggests breaking, so the result is unexpected — a contrast joined by 'but', as in Exercise 7.

mcqs.q: Ram Chand bowled well. He did not get a wicket. Join the sentences.
options: Ram Chand bowled well but he did not get a wicket.
Ram Chand bowled well and he got a wicket.
Ram Chand bowled well, wicket he got but.
Ram Chand bowled well or he did not get a wicket and.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Ram Chand bowled well but he did not get a wicket.' Bowling well and taking no wicket are contrasting ideas, from the matching and joining exercises.

mcqs.q: Razia washed her clothes. She cleaned her room. Join the sentences.
options: Razia washed her clothes, room cleaned she but.
Razia washed her clothes and cleaned her room.
Razia washed her clothes but cleaned her room not.
Razia washed her clothes or cleaned her room only one.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Razia washed her clothes and cleaned her room.' The two actions are similar and both done by Razia, so they are joined with 'and'.

mcqs.q: Which pair should be joined with 'and'?
options: I am short. My brother is very tall.
Their house is far. Our house is near.
He likes animals. He likes birds.
We take tea daily. We do not have ice cream daily.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'He likes animals. He likes birds.' Liking animals and liking birds are similar, adding ideas, joined in the book as 'He likes animals and birds.' The other pairs show contrasts and take 'but'.

mcqs.q: 'He has never climbed a mountain but he has climbed a tree.' Why is 'but' used here?
options: Because both actions are the same
Because the two ideas are different and contrasting
Because the sentence is a question
Because 'but' is used in every sentence
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that the two ideas are different and contrasting. Never climbing a mountain contrasts with having climbed a tree, so Exercise 8 joins the pair with 'but'.

lessons.title: Writing: Essay Writing
lessons.notes_html:
How an Essay Is Built

An essay has:

  • An introductory paragraph that introduces the topic.
  • Body paragraphs — at least two — each developing one main point.
  • A concluding paragraph that sums up the essay.

Model Essay: The Importance of Sports

Introduction: Sports are very popular all over the world. People of all ages play games and watch matches with great interest. Sports keep us healthy and teach us many good habits. The two most important benefits of sports are good health and good character.

Body 1 — Good health: Sports keep our bodies healthy and strong. When we play games, we run, jump and exercise, so our muscles grow strong and our hearts stay healthy. Playing games also keeps our minds fresh, and we can study better.

Body 2 — Good character: Players learn to follow rules, to work in a team, and to accept both victory and defeat. They learn discipline, patience and fair play, and they make good friends.

Conclusion: In short, sports give us both good health and good character. They make our bodies strong and our minds fresh, and they teach us discipline and teamwork. Every student should take part in sports every day.

Group Work

The essay is written in groups of 3, following the essay rules given in the unit: introductory paragraph, at least two body paragraphs, and a concluding paragraph.

mcqs.q: How many paragraphs must the essay on 'The Importance of Sports' have at least?
options: An introduction, at least two body paragraphs, and a conclusion
mcqs.why: The correct answer is an introductory paragraph, at least two body paragraphs, and a concluding paragraph. These are the essay rules given in the unit's writing task.

mcqs.q: In groups of how many is the essay written?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is groups of 3. The writing task says: 'In groups of 3, write an essay on the Importance of Sports...'

mcqs.q: What are the two most important benefits of sports named in the introduction?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is good health and good character. The model essay's introduction ends: 'The two most important benefits of sports are good health and good character,' and the two body paragraphs develop these two points.

mcqs.q: How do sports keep our bodies healthy, according to the essay?
options: By making us sleep all day
When we play, we run, jump and exercise, so muscles grow strong and hearts stay healthy
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that when we play games, we run, jump and exercise, so our muscles grow strong and our hearts stay healthy. The essay also says playing keeps our minds fresh so we can study better.

mcqs.q: What do players learn from sports, according to the second body paragraph?
options: To follow rules, work in a team, and accept both victory and defeat
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to follow rules, work in a team, and accept both victory and defeat. The paragraph adds that players learn discipline, patience and fair play, and make good friends.

mcqs.q: What does the concluding paragraph do?
options: Sums up the essay — sports give good health and good character, so every student should take part daily
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that it sums up the essay. The conclusion repeats the main idea briefly: sports make our bodies strong and minds fresh and teach discipline and teamwork, so every student should take part in sports every day.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is the best topic sentence for the health paragraph?
options: Sports keep our bodies healthy and strong.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Sports keep our bodies healthy and strong.' A topic sentence states the main idea of the whole paragraph, and the rest of that paragraph gives details about running, jumping, exercise, muscles and heart.

mcqs.q: Which of these does the essay say sports teach us?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is discipline and teamwork. The conclusion says sports 'teach us discipline and teamwork', and the body paragraph also mentions patience and fair play.

mcqs.q: Why can students study better if they play games?
options: Playing games keeps their minds fresh
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that playing games keeps their minds fresh. The essay's health paragraph says: 'Playing games also keeps our minds fresh, and we can study better.'

mcqs.q: What is the correct order of an essay's parts?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is introduction, body paragraphs, conclusion. This is the structure followed by the model essay on the Importance of Sports and required by the unit's essay rules.

lessons.title: Study Skills: Use of Dictionary
lessons.notes_html:
Using a Dictionary

A dictionary entry gives a word's meanings in order. In this unit we study the dictionary page for the word collapse.

The Word 'Collapse' — What the Dictionary Says

  • First meaning: of a building — to fall down suddenly, often after breaking apart.
  • For a sick person: to fall down (and usually become unconscious), especially because the person is very ill.
  • 'Fold' meaning: a folding table can be collapsed — folded into a shape that uses less space.
  • Sample sentence: "The roof collapsed under the weight of snow."
  • Collapsible: something that can be folded flat or made into a smaller shape that uses less space.

Three Regular Practices (Reminders in the Unit)

  • Do free writing regularly — it improves writing skills.
  • Practise cloze passages regularly — useful for learning English grammar and vocabulary.
  • Do some loud reading every day — reading aloud develops spoken language.

mcqs.q: What is the first meaning of 'collapse' in the dictionary?
options: Of a building, to fall down suddenly, often after breaking apart
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: of a building, to fall down suddenly, often after breaking apart. Dictionary meanings are given in order, and this is the first meaning on the page studied in the unit.

mcqs.q: What does 'collapse' mean when used for a sick person?
options: To fall down (and usually become unconscious) because the person is very ill
To break apart like a building
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to fall down (and usually become unconscious), especially because the person is very ill. The same word has different meanings for different subjects, which is why we read the whole dictionary entry.

mcqs.q: Can we collapse a folding table?
options: Yes — in the 'fold' sense, it can be folded into a shape that uses less space
mcqs.why: The correct answer is yes. The dictionary's 'fold' meaning allows it: a folding table can be folded into a shape that uses less space.

mcqs.q: Which is the dictionary's sample sentence for 'collapse'?
options: The roof collapsed under the weight of snow.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'The roof collapsed under the weight of snow.' This is the sample sentence given in the dictionary entry for 'collapse' in the unit.

mcqs.q: What does 'collapsible' mean?
options: That can be folded flat or made into a smaller shape that uses less space
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that it can be folded flat or made into a smaller shape that uses less space. 'Collapsible' is the adjective form connected with the 'fold' meaning of collapse.

mcqs.q: Why does a dictionary entry give more than one meaning for a word?
options: Because a word can be used in different senses for different subjects
Because the first meaning is always wrong
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that a word can be used in different senses for different subjects. 'Collapse' means one thing for a building, another for a sick person, and another for a folding table — the entry shows all of them.

mcqs.q: The unit reminds us that regular free writing ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that it improves our writing skills. Study Skills Exercise 2 says: 'Remember to do your free writing regularly as this will improve your writing skills.'

mcqs.q: Regular practice of cloze passages is very useful for learning ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is English grammar and vocabulary. This is the practice reminder given in Study Skills Exercise 3 of the unit.

mcqs.q: Why should we do loud reading every day?
options: Reading aloud helps develop our spoken language
It makes our voice louder only
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that reading aloud helps develop our spoken language. Study Skills Exercise 4 says: 'Make sure that you find time to do some loud reading every day.'

mcqs.q: To find the meaning of an unknown word like 'collapse', we should ______.
options: read its dictionary entry, including all meanings and the sample sentence
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to read its dictionary entry fully. In this unit, answering all five questions about 'collapse' is possible only by reading the complete entry — meanings, the sick-person sense, the fold sense and the sample sentence.

lessons.title: Fun: Creativity — Do and Do Not Charts
lessons.notes_html:
The Fun Activity

In groups of four, pupils prepare charts showing things that we should do and things that we should not do in four places: In the Class, In the School, In the Playground, In the Market.

Model Chart Points

  • In the Class — Do: listen to the teacher, raise your hand to speak, keep your desk clean. Do not: shout, disturb others, eat during the lesson.
  • In the School — Do: come on time, wear clean uniform, respect teachers and helpers. Do not: run in corridors, damage school property, bully others.
  • In the Playground — Do: play fairly, wait for your turn, help a fallen friend. Do not: push others, fight, leave litter.
  • In the Market — Do: walk on the footpath, buy only what you need, speak politely to shopkeepers. Do not: run across the road, touch things carelessly, waste money.

mcqs.q: In the Fun activity, pupils work in groups of ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is four. The book says: 'In groups of four, prepare charts showing things that we should do and things that we should not do...'

mcqs.q: The charts show ______.
options: the prices of things in the market
things we should do and things we should not do in given places
mcqs.why: The correct answer is things we should do and things we should not do in the given places. Each place gets a 'Do' list and a 'Do not' list.

mcqs.q: Which place is NOT one of the four places in the activity?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the hospital. The four places are: In the Class, In the School, In the Playground and In the Market.

mcqs.q: According to the model chart, what should we do in class?
options: Listen to the teacher and raise your hand to speak
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to listen to the teacher and raise your hand to speak. The 'Do' list for class also includes keeping your desk clean; shouting, disturbing others and eating during the lesson are on the 'Do not' list.

mcqs.q: Which is a 'Do not' for the school?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is running in corridors. The school 'Do not' list includes: do not run in corridors, do not damage school property, do not bully others.

mcqs.q: What should we do in the playground?
options: Play fairly and wait for your turn
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to play fairly and wait for your turn. Helping a fallen friend is also a 'Do'; pushing, fighting and leaving litter are 'Do nots'.

mcqs.q: What should we do in the market?
options: Walk on the footpath and buy only what we need
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to walk on the footpath and buy only what we need. The market 'Do' list also includes speaking politely to shopkeepers.

mcqs.q: Which behaviour belongs on the 'Do not' list for the market?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is wasting money. It appears in the market 'Do not' list along with running across the road and touching things carelessly.

mcqs.q: In class, 'keep your desk clean' is a ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a 'Do'. The class chart's 'Do' list is: listen to the teacher, raise your hand to speak, keep your desk clean.

mcqs.q: Helping a fallen friend in the playground is a ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a 'Do'. The playground 'Do' list is: play fairly, wait for your turn, help a fallen friend.

chapters.title: Awareness of and Empathy with Special People

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: The Blind Boy — A Poem
lessons.notes_html:
About the Poem

"The Blind Boy" is a poem by C. Cibber. In this poem a blind boy tells us how he feels. He was blind from birth, so he has never seen light and does not know the difference between light and darkness. Yet he is happy, because he cannot miss something he has never known — just as we do not miss the durian, the 'king of fruits', if we have never tasted it.

The Poem, Verse by Verse

  • Verse 1: The boy asks people what light is and what the blessings of sight are, because he will never be able to enjoy them.
  • Verse 2: People talk of wondrous (wonderful) things they see, like the bright sun. He can feel the sun's warmth but cannot understand how the sun makes day and night.
  • Verse 3: Since he cannot see the light, he makes his own day and night — as long as he stays awake, it is day for him; when he sleeps, it is night.
  • Verse 4: He hears people mourning (feeling sorry for) his hapless (unlucky) woe (sorrow) with heavy sighs. But he can bear this loss patiently, because he has never known what he is missing.
  • Verse 5: He requests people not to destroy his cheer (happiness) of mind by reminding him of what he cannot have. While he sings, he is a king, although he is a poor blind boy.

Word Meanings

  • blessings — favour from God
  • wondrous — wonderful
  • mourn — show sorrow over the loss of something
  • hapless — unlucky
  • woe — sorrow (misfortune / loss)
  • patience — accept suffering without complaint
  • cheer — joy (give happiness)

Short Forms in the Poem

  • call'd = called; ne'er = never; whene'er = whenever; 'twere = it were

True or False — Key Facts

  • The poem is about a blind boy (not a man) — True facts: he has never seen light; he can feel the sun but cannot see it; he has accepted that he will never see anything; he tells people not to feel sorry for him. False: he does sleep; he does not think people make fun of him.

The Main Idea

We should not make special (disabled) people unhappy by feeling pity for them. We should treat them with kindness and respect, as equals — help them when they need it (guiding a blind person across the road, describing things, reading to them) without making them feel helpless. We should let them be happy and enjoy their life.

mcqs.q: Who tells us his feelings in the poem 'The Blind Boy'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a blind boy. The summary in Exercise 9 begins: 'In this poem a blind boy tells us how he feels,' and the statement 'The blind boy's father is telling us the story' is marked 'No' in Exercise 1.

mcqs.q: Was the blind boy blind from birth?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is yes. Exercise 1 asks 'Was he blind from birth?' and the answer is 'Yes' — that is why he has never known what light is and cannot miss it.

mcqs.q: Did the blind boy know the difference between light and darkness?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is no. Exercise 1 gives the answer 'No' — he has never seen light, so for him there is no difference between day and night, and he makes his own day and night.

mcqs.q: Who wrote the poem 'The Blind Boy'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is C. Cibber. The gapped summary in Exercise 9 is completed: 'The title of the poem is The Blind Boy. It is written by C. Cibber.'

mcqs.q: What does the boy ask people in the first verse?
options: What light is and what the blessings of sight are
mcqs.why: The correct answer is what light is and what the blessings of sight are. The summary says: 'In the first verse he asks people what light is, because he will never enjoy it. He also asks what the blessings of sight are.'

mcqs.q: What can the boy feel, though he cannot see it?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the sun's warmth. Verse 2 says he feels the sun warm but cannot understand how it makes day or night, and the true/false exercise confirms: 'He can feel the sun but cannot see it' is True.

mcqs.q: How does the boy make his own day and night?
options: As long as he stays awake it is day for him; when he sleeps it is night
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that as long as he stays awake it is day for him, and when he sleeps it is night. This is the main point of verse 3, which is why he does not follow the sun's rising and setting.

mcqs.q: What does 'hapless' mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is unlucky. In Exercise 2, 'hapless' is matched with 'unlucky', and in Exercise 3 we read: 'In the final matches he always loses in a hapless manner.'

mcqs.q: What does 'patience' mean in the poem's vocabulary?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to accept suffering without complaint. 'Patience' is matched with this meaning in Exercise 2, and Exercise 3 uses it: 'We should show patience when old people do not understand what we say.'

mcqs.q: In which verse does the boy say he has no problem being blind because he does not know what he is losing?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is verse 4. Exercise 7 matches this point with verse 4 — this answer is given as the example in the book. In verse 4 he also says he can bear his loss patiently.

mcqs.q: What does the boy request people in the fifth verse?
options: Not to destroy his cheer of mind by reminding him that he is blind
mcqs.why: The correct answer is not to destroy his cheer (happiness) of mind by reminding him of what he cannot have. The matching exercise adds that as long as he can happily accept his situation, he can enjoy life — while he sings, he is a king.

mcqs.q: Why is it difficult for the blind boy to understand how the sun makes day and night?
options: He has never seen light or darkness, so he cannot understand how sunlight changes night into day
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that he has never seen light or darkness. Exercise 10 gives this model answer: he cannot imagine what light is like because he has never experienced it — the same idea as the pre-reading discussion about babies born without sight.

mcqs.q: Do you think the blind boy is happy? Choose the answer the book supports.
options: Yes — he accepts his blindness patiently, sings, and says that while he sings he is a king
No, he is angry with everyone
No, he cries all the time
mcqs.why: The correct answer is yes, he is happy. Exercise 10's model answer explains: he accepts his blindness patiently, he sings, and he says that while he sings he is a king — so Exercise 1 also answers 'Was he happy? — Yes.'

mcqs.q: What is the main idea of the poem?
options: We should feel pity for disabled people all the time
We should not make special people unhappy by feeling pity for them; let them be happy and enjoy life
We should not talk to blind people
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that we should not make special (disabled) people unhappy by feeling pity for them; we should let them be happy and let them enjoy their life happily. This is the main idea completed in the summary of Exercise 9.

mcqs.q: How should we help blind people, according to the discussion answers?
options: By guiding them across the road, describing things and reading to them, without making them feel helpless
By doing everything for them and making them feel helpless
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to help when needed — guiding across the road, describing things, reading to them and keeping places safe — without making them feel helpless. We should treat people with any disability with kindness and respect, as equals.

lessons.title: Speaking: Expressing Surprise
lessons.notes_html:
What We Practise

In section 4.2 we practise expressing surprise. Pupils work in groups of three, practise the given dialogue, and then write and practise their own six-line dialogue with changed roles.

Surprise Words and Expressions

  • Oh my God!
  • That's wonderful!
  • That's very sad!
  • Good news!
  • We've won!
  • Oh, no! I don't believe this!
  • Oh! Poor thing!
  • Wow!

A Model Dialogue

  • A: Did you know that Ali won first prize in the race?
  • B: Wow! That's wonderful! How did he win?
  • A: He ran very fast and never stopped.
  • C: Oh! That's great! I am so happy for him!
  • B: By the way, did you hear that our class will go on a trip?
  • C: Oh my God! That's good news! We've won a trip!

Remember

Surprise expressions can show happiness ("Wow! That's wonderful!"), sadness ("Oh! Poor thing!", "That's very sad!") or disbelief ("Oh, no! I don't believe this!"). Choose the expression that matches the news.

mcqs.q: What speaking skill is practised in section 4.2?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is expressing surprise. The section title is 'Speaking: Express Surprise', and pupils practise a dialogue full of surprise expressions.

mcqs.q: Pupils practise the dialogue in groups of ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is three. The exercise says: 'In groups of three, practise the given dialogue expressing surprise...'

mcqs.q: How long should the pupils' own dialogue be?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is six lines. After practising the given dialogue, groups 'discuss and write a six-line dialogue like it, using surprise words', and practise it with changed roles.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an expression of surprise?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Oh my God! That's wonderful!' It is one of the surprise expressions listed in the book, used when we hear happy and unexpected news.

mcqs.q: Which expression shows surprise at sad news?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Oh! Poor thing!' The book lists it among surprise words for sad news, together with 'That's very sad!', while 'We've won!' and 'That's wonderful!' are for happy news.

mcqs.q: Which expression shows that we cannot believe the news?
options: Oh, no! I don't believe this!
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Oh, no! I don't believe this!' This expression from the book's list shows disbelief — the news is so surprising that it is hard to believe.

mcqs.q: In the model dialogue, how does B reply to the news that Ali won first prize in the race?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Wow! That's wonderful!' Winning first prize is happy news, so the joyful surprise expressions 'Wow!' and 'That's wonderful!' fit it.

mcqs.q: Which expression fits the news that the class will go on a trip?
options: Oh my God! That's good news!
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Oh my God! That's good news!' In the model dialogue, C reacts to the trip news with exactly these words and adds 'We've won a trip!'

mcqs.q: After writing their own dialogue, what should the groups do with it?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to practise it with changed roles. The exercise ends: 'Practise it with changed roles,' so that every pupil speaks different lines.

mcqs.q: Which sentence uses a surprise expression correctly?
options: Hearing a joke, Aslam said, 'Write your name.'
Hearing good news, Aslam said, 'Please open page ten.'
Hearing that his friend was ill, Aslam said, 'Oh! Poor thing!'
Hearing that they won, Aslam said, 'Sit down quietly.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Oh! Poor thing!' for a friend's illness. Surprise expressions must match the feeling of the news — 'Poor thing' expresses sympathy and surprise at sad news, as listed in the book.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Forming Adjectives
lessons.notes_html:
Making Adjectives by Adding a Suffix

Many adjectives are made from nouns by adding a suffix:

  • -less (without): end → endless, job → jobless, aim → aimless, tree → treeless
  • -ful (full of): harm → harmful, peace → peaceful, hope → hopeful, care → careful
  • -y: wind → windy, air → airy, dirt → dirty, powder → powdery, salt → salty
  • -ly: ghost → ghostly, mother → motherly, hour → hourly, friend → friendly
  • -ish: child → childish, fool → foolish, book → bookish

Using the Adjectives (Exercise 2)

  • In the treeless desert the travellers could not find a shady place.
  • Every citizen wants to lead a peaceful life, without fear and worries.
  • The dirty clothes of the children show they have been playing in the garden.
  • My new neighbours are very friendly people.
  • We need both practical and bookish knowledge.
  • Do not lead an aimless life.
  • Careful drivers always drive within the speed limit.
  • We have very windy weather today.
  • Some schools have an hourly time table.
  • People in Gilgit Baltistan drink salty tea.

mcqs.q: The adjective formed from 'end' is ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'endless'. Adding the suffix '-less' (meaning 'without') to 'end' gives 'endless', as in the first group of Exercise 1, like 'jobless', 'aimless' and 'treeless'.

mcqs.q: The adjective formed from 'peace' is ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'peaceful'. The suffix '-ful' means 'full of': harm → harmful, hope → hopeful, care → careful, peace → peaceful. In Exercise 2, 'every citizen wants to lead a peaceful life'.

mcqs.q: The adjective formed from 'wind' is ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'windy'. The suffix '-y' forms windy, airy, dirty, powdery and salty. Exercise 2 says: 'We have very windy weather today.'

mcqs.q: The adjective formed from 'friend' is ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'friendly'. The suffix '-ly' gives ghostly, motherly, hourly and friendly. Exercise 2 uses it: 'I like my new neighbours because they are very friendly people.'

mcqs.q: The adjective formed from 'child' is ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'childish'. The suffix '-ish' forms childish, foolish and bookish, as shown in the last group of Exercise 1.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'In the ______ desert, the travellers could not find any shady place to rest.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'treeless'. A desert without trees has no shade, so 'treeless' (tree + -less) is the suitable adjective in Exercise 2.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: '______ drivers always drive the car within the speed limit.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Careful'. Drivers who take care and follow the speed limit are careful drivers (care + -ful), as in Exercise 2.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'People in Gilgit Baltistan drink ______ tea.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'salty'. Exercise 2's sentence contrasts sweet tea with the salty tea (salt + -y) drunk in Gilgit Baltistan.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'We need both practical and ______ knowledge to succeed in life.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'bookish'. Bookish knowledge is knowledge from books, and the sentence contrasts it with practical knowledge, as given in Exercise 2.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'Decide what you want to do in life. Do not lead an ______ life.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'aimless'. A life without an aim or purpose is aimless (aim + -less), which is why the book advises us to decide what we want to do.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Question Words — Yes/No and Wh- Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Main Verbs and Helping Verbs

  • "The horse is eating grass." — helping verb: is; main verb: eating.
  • "Saba can sing beautifully." — helping verb: can; main verb: sing.
  • "We have eaten our food." — helping verb: have; main verb: eaten.
  • Some sentences have no helping verb: "We love Pakistan." / "I am a teacher." / "The train is late." / "My sister buys new books every year." (Here am/is/was/buys/love are main verbs.)

Making Yes/No Questions

Put the helping verb (or a form of do/does) at the beginning:

  • The horse is eating grass → Is the horse eating grass?
  • We love Pakistan → Do we love Pakistan?
  • My sister buys new books → Does my sister buy new books every year?
  • Tahir and Javed will go → Will Tahir and Javed go to Lahore?

Making Wh- Questions

Use question words — what, where, who, how, when — before the helping verb:

  • What is the horse eating? / How can Saba sing? / Where will Tahir and Javed go?
  • Who was lost? (The old man was lost.) / What does my sister buy every year?
  • What are you wearing? / How are you feeling? / Who is the teacher helping?

mcqs.q: In 'The horse is eating grass', the helping verb is ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'is'. In Exercise 4, 'is' is underlined once as the helping verb and 'eating' twice as the main verb. Helping verbs like is, can, will and have stand with a main verb.

mcqs.q: In 'We love Pakistan', the main verb is ______ and there is ______ helping verb.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'love', with no helping verb. Exercise 4 notes that sentences like 'We love Pakistan', 'I am a teacher' and 'The train is late' have only a main verb.

mcqs.q: Change into a Yes/No question: 'The train is late.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Is the train late?' For a Yes/No question, the helping/main verb 'is' moves to the beginning, as shown in Exercise 5.

mcqs.q: Change into a Yes/No question: 'My sister buys new books every year.'
options: Does my sister buy new books every year?
Buys my sister new books every year?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Does my sister buy new books every year?' The sentence has no helping verb, so 'does' is added and 'buys' becomes 'buy', exactly as in Exercise 5.

mcqs.q: Change into a Yes/No question: 'Saba can sing beautifully.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Can Saba sing beautifully?' The helping verb 'can' comes to the front to make a Yes/No question, as in Exercise 5.

mcqs.q: Form a Wh- question for: 'The horse is eating grass.' (answer: grass)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'What is the horse eating?' Exercise 6 forms Wh- questions from the same statements; since the answer is a thing (grass), the question word is 'what'.

mcqs.q: Form a Wh- question for: 'Tahir and Javed will go to Lahore.' (answer: Lahore)
options: Where will Tahir and Javed go?
When will Tahir and Javed go?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Where will Tahir and Javed go?' The answer is a place (Lahore), so the question word is 'where', as in the model answers of Exercise 6.

mcqs.q: Form a Wh- question for: 'The old man was lost.' (answer: the old man)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Who was lost?' The answer is a person, so we ask with 'who', following the pattern of Exercise 6.

mcqs.q: Change into a Yes/No question: 'The blind old man needs help.'
options: Needs the blind old man help?
Is the blind old man needs help?
Does the blind old man need help?
What does the blind old man need?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Does the blind old man need help?' Exercise 7 directs this one as a Y/N question, so 'does' is added and 'needs' becomes 'need'.

mcqs.q: Form a Wh- question for: 'I am feeling very hungry and thirsty.' (answer: how you are feeling)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'How are you feeling?' When the answer describes a state or manner, we ask with 'how'; Exercise 7 gives this model answer.

lessons.title: Writing: Essay Writing — Main Idea and Details
lessons.notes_html:
Finding the Main Idea of a Paragraph

Every paragraph has a main idea, and the other sentences give details that support it. In this unit we read a sample essay on Pollution and identify the main idea and supporting details of each paragraph:

  • Paragraph 1 (Introduction): Pollution is a very big problem; there are many types of pollution caused by various factors. Details: people all over the world have health issues because of it; pollution means an unclean environment.
  • Paragraph 2: There are three main types of pollution. Details: air pollution from smoke of factories and vehicles; noise pollution from loudspeakers and horns; water pollution from dirty chemical and human waste thrown in rivers and seas.
  • Paragraph 3: Pollution damages people's health. Details: dreadful diseases like cancer, asthma and liver problems; stress diseases like diabetes and heart problems.
  • Paragraph 4: Citizens must play their role in stopping pollution. Details: do not throw garbage everywhere; stop vehicles emitting black fumes; do not throw waste in ponds and rivers; do not blow horns loudly, play loud music or fire gunshots.
  • Paragraph 5: The government must also take steps. Details: enforce laws; impose fines; reward factories that control waste; reward tree planting; strictly prohibit cutting trees; show awareness programmes on television.
  • Paragraph 6 (Conclusion): Both citizens and the government need to act together; only then can we overcome the problem.

Writing a Cause and Effect Essay

The unit's own writing task is a cause and effect essay on the problems in our education system. The model essay names three major problems and gives the effect of each:

  • Untrained teachers — lessons are dull, students lose interest, results become poor.
  • Rote learning — students memorise without understanding; they pass exams but cannot use knowledge in real life.
  • Lack of facilities — crowded classrooms, no libraries, no clean drinking water, no laboratories; students cannot learn properly and many leave school early.
  • Conclusion: if the government trains teachers, changes examinations and provides facilities, our schools will improve.

mcqs.q: What is the main idea of Paragraph 2 of the sample essay on Pollution?
options: There are three main types of pollution
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that there are three main types of pollution. The details support it: air pollution from smoke of factories and vehicles, noise pollution from loudspeakers and horns, and water pollution from waste thrown in rivers and seas.

mcqs.q: Which diseases are mentioned as details in the health paragraph (Paragraph 3)?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is cancer, asthma and liver problems. Paragraph 3's main idea is that pollution damages people's health, and it also mentions stress diseases like diabetes and heart problems.

mcqs.q: What must citizens do, according to Paragraph 4?
options: Not throw waste in ponds and rivers, and not blow horns loudly
mcqs.why: The correct answer is not to throw waste in ponds and rivers and not to blow horns loudly. Paragraph 4's main idea is that citizens must play their role in stopping pollution; it also says to stop vehicles emitting black fumes.

mcqs.q: Which step belongs to the government's role in Paragraph 5?
options: Enforce laws and impose fines on polluters
Throw garbage in bins at home
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to enforce laws and impose fines. Paragraph 5 also lists rewarding factories that control waste, rewarding tree planting, prohibiting cutting trees and showing awareness programmes on television.

mcqs.q: What does the conclusion (Paragraph 6) of the sample essay say?
options: Both citizens and the government need to act together
Only the government can stop pollution
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that both citizens and the government need to act together. Only if citizens take responsibility and the government has strict rules can we overcome the problem.

mcqs.q: In the model essay on education, which is NOT one of the three major problems?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is too many holidays. The model essay names untrained teachers, rote learning and a lack of facilities as the three major problems in our education system.

mcqs.q: What is the effect of untrained teachers, according to the model essay?
options: Lessons are dull, students lose interest and their results become poor
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that lessons are dull, students lose interest in learning and their results become poor. A cause and effect essay always joins each problem (cause) with what it leads to (effect), like this example.

mcqs.q: What is the effect of rote learning?
options: Students pass examinations but cannot use their knowledge in real life
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that students pass examinations but cannot use their knowledge in real life. The essay explains that students memorise books without understanding because examinations only test memory.

mcqs.q: Which facilities are missing in many schools, according to the essay?
options: Libraries, clean drinking water and science laboratories
mcqs.why: The correct answer is libraries, clean drinking water and science laboratories. The essay also mentions crowded classrooms, and says that because of this lack, students cannot learn properly and many leave school early.

mcqs.q: According to the essay's conclusion, our schools will improve if the government ______.
options: trains teachers, changes examinations and provides facilities
mcqs.why: The correct answer is trains teachers, changes examinations and provides facilities. Each solution in the conclusion answers one of the three problems named in the essay — this is how a cause and effect essay is summed up.

lessons.title: Study Skills: Blurbs
lessons.notes_html:
What Is a Blurb?

A blurb is the short text on the cover of a book that tells us what the book is about, so that readers can decide whether to read it. In this unit we read the cover of a book by Roald Dahl, the famous writer of children's books (the book prints "Roald Dhal" — a typo).

The Blurb of 'James and the Giant Peach'

  • The boy in the book is James Trotter (James).
  • James's parents were eaten by an enormous escaped rhinoceros from London Zoo, according to the blurb.

Three Regular Practices (Reminders in the Unit)

  • Do free writing regularly — it improves writing skills.
  • Practise cloze passages regularly — useful for learning English grammar and vocabulary.
  • Do some loud reading every day — reading aloud develops spoken language.

mcqs.q: What is a blurb?
options: The price tag of a book
The short text on a book's cover telling what the book is about
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the short text on a book's cover telling what the book is about. In Study Skills we read a book cover and answer questions 'according to the blurb'.

mcqs.q: According to the blurb, what is the name of the boy in Roald Dahl's book?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is James Trotter. He is the hero of 'James and the Giant Peach', as the blurb on the cover tells us. (The book prints the author's name as 'Roald Dhal', a typo for Roald Dahl.)

mcqs.q: Who ate the parents of James, according to the blurb?
options: An enormous escaped rhinoceros from London Zoo
mcqs.why: The correct answer is an enormous escaped rhinoceros from London Zoo. This surprising detail is exactly what the blurb says, and it is the kind of exciting information a blurb uses to attract readers.

mcqs.q: Roald Dahl is famous as a writer of ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is children's books. The exercise introduces him as 'Roald Dahl, the famous writer of children's books'.

mcqs.q: What is the blurb of this book printed on?
options: The cover page of the book
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the cover page. The exercise says: 'Read the cover page of the book written by Roald Dahl... According to the blurb...' — blurbs appear on book covers.

mcqs.q: Why do books have blurbs?
options: To give the answers of exercises
To tell readers what the book is about so they can choose it
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to tell readers what the book is about so they can choose it. From James's blurb we learn the hero's name and the strange death of his parents — enough to make a reader curious.

mcqs.q: The unit reminds us to do free writing regularly because it ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that it improves our writing skills. Study Skills Exercise 2 of this unit repeats the reminder first given in Unit 3.

mcqs.q: Regular practice of cloze passages is useful for learning ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is English grammar and vocabulary. This is the reminder in Study Skills Exercise 3 of this unit.

mcqs.q: What daily practice develops our spoken language?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is loud reading every day. Study Skills Exercise 4 says: 'Make sure that you find time to do some loud reading every day. Reading aloud will help you develop your spoken language.'

mcqs.q: Which question can a blurb answer?
options: What is the price of paper?
What is the book about and who is its main character?
How many schools use the book?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is what the book is about and who its main character is. Both Study Skills questions in this unit — the boy's name and what happened to his parents — are answered from the blurb alone.

lessons.title: Fun: Creativity — Programming a Robot to Help the Blind
lessons.notes_html:
The Fun Activity

Imagine you get a job in a company that makes robots. Your job is to programme the robot to help people who are blind. Work in groups of three and design a programme for the robot in any one of these areas:

  • washing the dishes
  • flying a kite
  • polishing shoes
  • playing cricket
  • using a mobile phone
  • putting things in a bag

Then roleplay: one pupil acts like a robot, one like a blind person, and one reads the instructions.

Model Programme — Washing the Dishes

  • Step 1: Go to the kitchen sink.
  • Step 2: Turn on the warm water tap.
  • Step 3: Put one drop of washing liquid on the sponge.
  • Step 4: Pick up one plate with your left hand.
  • Step 5: Rub the plate gently with the sponge in small circles.
  • Step 6: Rinse the plate under clean water.
  • Step 7: Put the clean plate on the drying rack.
  • Step 8: Repeat steps 4 to 7 for every plate, cup and spoon.
  • Step 9: Turn off the tap.
  • Step 10: Tell the person, "The dishes are washed."

Remember

A programme is a list of clear steps in the right order. Each step must be exact — for example, how much washing liquid (one drop), which hand (left), and how to rub (gently, in small circles) — because a robot follows instructions exactly, and its user cannot see.

mcqs.q: In the Fun activity, your job is to programme a robot to help ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is people who are blind. The activity says: 'Your job is to programme the robot to help people who are blind,' which connects the Fun section with the unit's theme of empathy with special people.

mcqs.q: In groups of how many do pupils design the robot programme?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is three. The book says: 'Work in groups of three and design a programme for the robot in any one area.'

mcqs.q: Which of these is one of the areas given in the book?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is washing the dishes. The six areas are: washing the dishes, flying a kite, polishing shoes, playing cricket, using a mobile phone, and putting things in a bag.

mcqs.q: In the roleplay, what are the three roles?
options: A cook, a waiter and a guest
One acts like a robot, one like a blind person, one reads the instructions
A teacher, a student and a parent
mcqs.why: The correct answer is one robot, one blind person, and one reader of instructions. The book says: 'Then roleplay: one acts like a robot, one like a blind person, one reads the instructions.'

mcqs.q: What is Step 1 of the model dish-washing programme?
options: Turn on the warm water tap
Put washing liquid on the sponge
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Go to the kitchen sink.' A programme must begin at the right starting point; only then does the robot turn on the warm water tap in Step 2.

mcqs.q: How much washing liquid does the robot put on the sponge in Step 3?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is one drop. Programme instructions must be exact: 'Put one drop of washing liquid on the sponge.' A robot follows instructions exactly as given.

mcqs.q: With which hand does the robot pick up the plate, and how does it rub it?
options: Left hand; rub gently with the sponge in small circles
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the left hand, rubbing gently in small circles. Steps 4 and 5 of the model programme give these exact details because the robot — and its blind user — need precise instructions.

mcqs.q: What does the robot do after rinsing a plate?
options: Puts the clean plate on the drying rack
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to put the clean plate on the drying rack. This is Step 7, and Steps 4 to 7 are then repeated for every plate, cup and spoon.

mcqs.q: What is the last step of the model programme?
options: Tell the person, 'The dishes are washed.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to tell the person, 'The dishes are washed.' After turning off the tap in Step 9, the robot informs the blind person in Step 10 that the work is complete — important because the person cannot see the result.

mcqs.q: Why must a robot programme give steps in exact order with exact details?
options: Because longer programmes get more marks
Because a robot follows instructions exactly, and the blind user cannot check the work by seeing it
Because the steps are a poem
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that a robot follows instructions exactly, and the blind user cannot check by seeing. That is why the model programme says one drop, left hand, small circles, and ends by announcing that the dishes are washed.

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: Pakistan — Home to Ancient Civilization
lessons.notes_html:
About the Lesson

You are going on a helicopter tour of Pakistan's ancient historical places. The tour takes two days. You visit seven ancient sites. These sites show that Pakistan is home to one of the oldest civilizations in the world — the Indus Valley Civilization.

The Seven Sites

  • Bhambore (Sindh) — where Muhammad bin Qasim entered Sindh; the ruins mention the Raja Dahir era.
  • Mohenjo-Daro (Sindh) — a city about 5,000 years old; the largest city of the Indus Valley Civilization; famous for the Great Bath, the Stupa and the statue of the Priest King; excavated by R. D. Bannerji; a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
  • Nindowari (Balochistan) — also called Nal; belongs to the Kulli culture, older than the Indus Valley Civilization; famous for the Kulli stoneware pottery style.
  • Harappa (Punjab) — about 4,500 years old; famous for the ancient citadel, the drain system, handcraft items and the Working Platform.
  • Taxila (Punjab) — called "The City of Cut Stone"; its name comes from Takshaka, the mythical serpent-king; home of the Dharmarajika Stupa.
  • Rehman Dheri (Khyber Pakhtunkhwa) — the oldest planned city in South Asia, about 5,500 years old; famous for pottery work at Kot Diji.
  • Takht-i-Bahi (Khyber Pakhtunkhwa) — the best-preserved and largest Buddhist monastery complex in Gandhara; founded in the 1st century AD; 'Takht' means "throne of origins"; a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

How the Sites Are Counted by Province

  • Sindh — 2 sites (Bhambore, Mohenjo-Daro)
  • Balochistan — 1 site (Nindowari)
  • Punjab — 2 sites (Harappa, Taxila)
  • Khyber Pakhtunkhwa — 2 sites (Rehman Dheri, Takht-i-Bahi)

When Were the Sites Founded? (Exercises)

  • Rehman Dheri — about 3500 BC
  • Mohenjo-Daro — about 2600 BC
  • Bhambore — 1st century BC
  • Taxila — 6th century BC (some scholars say 1000 BC)
  • Harappa — about 1900 BC
  • Takht-i-Bahi — 1st century AD

Famous Things at Each Site

  • Mohenjo-Daro — Stupa, Great Bath, Priest King statue
  • Harappa — Working Platform, drains, citadel
  • Bhambore — ruins connected with Muhammad bin Qasim and Raja Dahir
  • Nindowari — Kulli stoneware pottery
  • Rehman Dheri — Kot Diji pottery
  • Taxila — Dharmarajika Stupa
  • Takht-i-Bahi — Buddhist monastery remains

Why These Places Matter

These sites are the cultural heritage and identity of Pakistan. They are important for tourism and for the economy, and they teach us about our history and traditions. We should protect and preserve them: keep them clean, do not damage or write on the walls, follow the rules, and spread awareness.

mcqs.q: How many places in Pakistan will the class visit on the helicopter tour?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is seven. The pre-reading answer says: 'You will visit seven places in Pakistan,' and the exercises list Bhambore, Mohenjo-Daro, Nindowari, Harappa, Taxila, Rehman Dheri and Takht-i-Bahi.

mcqs.q: How many days will the tour take?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is two days. The pre-reading exercise asks 'How many days will you take to tour Pakistan?' and the answer given is 'Two days.'

mcqs.q: Which province has only one site on the tour?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Balochistan. The counting exercise shows Sindh 2, Balochistan 1, Punjab 2 and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa 2 — Balochistan's only site is Nindowari.

mcqs.q: Which site is famous for the Great Bath, the Stupa and the statue of the Priest King?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Mohenjo-Daro. The famous-things exercise lists for Mohenjo-Daro: 'Stupa, Great Bath, Priest King.' It is the largest city of the Indus Valley Civilization, excavated by R. D. Bannerji.

mcqs.q: Which site is called 'The City of Cut Stone'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Taxila. Its other names are also given: the name comes from Takshaka, a serpent-king in Hindu mythology, and it is called 'The City of Cut Stone'.

mcqs.q: What is Takht-i-Bahi famous for?
options: Being the best-preserved and largest Buddhist monastery complex in Gandhara
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Buddhist monastery complex. The exercise says Takht-i-Bahi is 'the best preserved and the largest Buddhist monastery complex in Gandhara', founded in the 1st century AD.

mcqs.q: Which of these pairs (site — famous thing) is WRONG?
options: Harappa — Working Platform and drain system
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Bhambore — Great Bath'. The Great Bath belongs to Mohenjo-Daro; Bhambore is famous as the place where Muhammad bin Qasim entered Sindh, with ruins of the Raja Dahir era.

mcqs.q: Which is the oldest site on the tour, the oldest planned city in South Asia?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Rehman Dheri. The dating exercise puts it at about 3500 BC and calls it the oldest planned city in South Asia, older than Mohenjo-Daro (2600 BC) and Harappa (1900 BC).

mcqs.q: What does 'Takht' mean in Takht-i-Bahi?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'throne of origins'. The while-reading exercise asks exactly this: 'What does Takht mean? — Throne of origins.'

mcqs.q: Which two sites on the tour are UNESCO World Heritage Sites?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Mohenjo-Daro and Takht-i-Bahi. The matching exercises give UNESCO World Heritage Site status to both of them.

mcqs.q: In which province is Nindowari (Nal) located?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Balochistan. The province-matching exercise places Nindowari in Balochistan; it belongs to the Kulli culture, which is older than the Indus Valley Civilization.

mcqs.q: The Kulli culture of Nindowari is ______ than the Indus Valley Civilization.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is older. The exercise states that the Kulli culture is older than the Indus Valley Civilization, and Nindowari is famous for its Kulli stoneware pottery style.

mcqs.q: Why are these historical places important for Pakistan?
options: They are our cultural heritage and identity, important for tourism, the economy and learning our history
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that they are our cultural heritage and identity. The model answer adds that they bring tourists, support the economy and teach us about our history and traditions.

mcqs.q: How should we protect these historical places?
options: By keeping them clean, not damaging them, following the rules and spreading awareness
By writing our names on their walls
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to keep them clean, not damage them, follow the rules and spread awareness. The post-reading model answer lists exactly these duties for every citizen.

mcqs.q: Which sentence about Harappa is TRUE?
options: It is about 4,500 years old and famous for its citadel, drain system and Working Platform
It was founded in the 1st century AD
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that Harappa is about 4,500 years old and famous for its citadel, drain system and Working Platform. It is in Punjab, and the 1st century AD date belongs to Takht-i-Bahi.

lessons.title: Speaking: Expressing Pleasure and Displeasure
lessons.notes_html:
What We Practise

In section 5.2 we practise expressing pleasure and displeasure. Pleasure means feelings of happiness and satisfaction; displeasure means feelings of unhappiness and dissatisfaction.

A Model Dialogue

  • Aqsa: Hi, Fatima! How are you?
  • Fatima: I am fine, thank you. Look at this new dress my mother bought for me!
  • Aqsa: Wow! It is beautiful! I really like the colours. (expressing pleasure)
  • Fatima: Thank you! I am so happy with it. (expressing pleasure)
  • Aqsa: But I am sorry, I broke your favourite vase yesterday. (expressing displeasure — unhappy news)
  • Fatima: Oh no! I am really upset about that. That vase was a gift from my grandmother. (expressing displeasure)
  • Aqsa: I am very sorry. I will buy you a new one.
  • Fatima: It is okay. Accidents happen. (forgiving)

Expressions of Pleasure

  • Wow! It is beautiful!
  • I am so happy!
  • That is wonderful!
  • I really like it!
  • Great!

Expressions of Displeasure

  • Oh no!
  • I am really upset about that.
  • That is terrible!
  • I do not like it at all.
  • How disappointing!

Remember

When we break or spoil something belonging to another person, we should say sorry honestly, like Aqsa does — and the other person may forgive us, because accidents happen.

mcqs.q: What speaking skill is practised in section 5.2?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is expressing pleasure and displeasure. The section title is 'Speaking: Expressing Pleasure and Displeasure', and the model dialogue shows both feelings.

mcqs.q: In the model dialogue, why is Fatima happy at the start?
options: Her friend gave her a vase
She is going on a tour
Her mother bought her a new dress
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that her mother bought her a new dress. Fatima says, 'Look at this new dress my mother bought for me!' and Aqsa replies, 'Wow! It is beautiful!'

mcqs.q: Which expression shows pleasure?
options: I am really upset about that.
Wow! It is beautiful! I am so happy!
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Wow! It is beautiful! I am so happy!' Expressions of pleasure show happiness and satisfaction, while 'upset', 'Oh no!' and 'terrible' show displeasure.

mcqs.q: What bad news does Aqsa give in the dialogue?
options: She broke Fatima's favourite vase yesterday
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that she broke Fatima's favourite vase yesterday. She says sorry honestly: 'But I am sorry, I broke your favourite vase yesterday.'

mcqs.q: Why was the vase special for Fatima?
options: It was a gift from her grandmother
It was very old and golden
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that it was a gift from her grandmother. That is why Fatima says, 'I am really upset about that. That vase was a gift from my grandmother.'

mcqs.q: Which expression shows displeasure?
options: I am really upset about that.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'I am really upset about that.' Displeasure means feelings of unhappiness and dissatisfaction — the opposite of pleasure.

mcqs.q: What does Aqsa promise after breaking the vase?
options: To buy Fatima a new one
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to buy Fatima a new one. Aqsa says, 'I am very sorry. I will buy you a new one.' Saying sorry and offering to replace what we broke is the polite way to handle such a mistake.

mcqs.q: How does Fatima finally respond to Aqsa's apology?
options: She says, 'It is okay. Accidents happen.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'It is okay. Accidents happen.' Fatima forgives Aqsa because Aqsa was honest and sorry — the dialogue ends kindly, which is the model for handling displeasure politely.

mcqs.q: Your friend shows you his new bicycle. Which reply expresses pleasure?
options: Wow! It is wonderful! I really like it!
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Wow! It is wonderful! I really like it!' A friend's new bicycle is happy news, so we express pleasure, just as Aqsa does for Fatima's new dress.

mcqs.q: Your younger brother has spoilt your notebook. Which sentence expresses displeasure politely?
options: Oh no! I am really upset about that. Please be careful with my things.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Oh no! I am really upset about that. Please be careful with my things.' It expresses displeasure honestly but politely, the way the model dialogue teaches — displeasure without rudeness.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Verb Forms and the Present Perfect Tense
lessons.notes_html:
Verb Forms

Every verb has forms we must know. Examples from the exercises:

  • write — wrote — written (write a letter — wrote a letter — has written a letter)
  • speak — spoke — spoken; bring — brought — brought; fly — flew — flown; see — saw — seen; make — made — made; take — took — taken; sing — sang — sung; ride — rode — ridden; ring — rang — rung; swim — swam — swum; drink — drank — drunk; begin — began — begun; do — did — done; go — went — gone; come — came — come; run — ran — run; read — read — read

The Present Perfect Tense

Form: subject + has/have + past participle (3rd form). We use has with he/she/it and singular nouns, and have with I/we/you/they and plural nouns.

  • She has eaten lunch. / They have finished their homework.
  • He has gone to school. / I have seen this film.
  • We use it for actions completed at an unstated time in the past, often with already, just, ever, never: Have you ever been to Lahore? I have never flown in an aeroplane.

Negatives and Questions

  • Negative: subject + has/have + not + past participle — She has not come yet.
  • Question: Has/Have + subject + past participle? — Have you done your work?

Use the Correct Form (from the exercises)

  • The train has just left the station. (leave)
  • Ali has broken his leg. (break)
  • We have visited Karachi twice. (visit)
  • The baby has drunk all the milk. (drink)
  • They have built a new school. (build)
  • He has not written a letter yet. (write)

mcqs.q: What is the past participle (3rd form) of 'write'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'written'. The three forms are write — wrote — written, so the present perfect is 'has written', as in 'She has written a letter.'

mcqs.q: What is the past participle of 'fly'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'flown'. Fly — flew — flown. In the present perfect we say 'The bird has flown away', never 'has flew', because the third form follows has/have.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'She has eaten lunch.' With 'she' we use 'has', and after has/have we use the past participle 'eaten' (eat — ate — eaten), not the past form 'ate'.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'They have finished their homework.' Plural subjects like 'they' take 'have', and 'finished' is the past participle of the regular verb 'finish'.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'The train ______ just ______ the station.' (leave)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'has left'. The train is singular, so 'has' is used, and the past participle of leave is 'left'. 'Just' is a common present-perfect word showing a very recent action.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'Ali ______ ______ his leg.' (break)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'has broken'. Ali is singular (has), and the past participle of break is 'broken' (break — broke — broken).

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'We ______ ______ Karachi twice.' (visit)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'have visited'. 'We' takes 'have', and the past participle of the regular verb 'visit' is 'visited'. The word 'twice' shows experience up to now, a present-perfect use.

mcqs.q: What is the past participle of 'drink'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'drunk'. Drink — drank — drunk, so we say 'The baby has drunk all the milk.'

mcqs.q: Make the negative: 'She has come.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'She has not come yet.' In the present perfect, 'not' comes between has/have and the past participle: has + not + come.

mcqs.q: Make the question: 'You have done your work.'
options: Do you have done your work?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Have you done your work?' Present-perfect questions begin with Has/Have, followed by the subject and the past participle.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'Have you ______ been to Lahore?'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'ever'. In questions about life experience we use 'ever': 'Have you ever been to Lahore?' Its negative partner is 'never': 'I have never flown in an aeroplane.'

mcqs.q: What is the past participle of 'see'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'seen'. See — saw — seen, so the present perfect is 'I have seen this film.'

mcqs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'He has gone to school.' Go — went — gone; after 'has' we must use 'gone', and singular 'he' takes 'has', not 'have'.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'They ______ ______ a new school in our village.' (build)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'have built'. 'They' takes 'have', and the past participle of build is 'built' (build — built — built), not 'builded'.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is in the present perfect tense?
options: She writes a letter every day.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'She has written a letter.' Has/have + past participle (written) makes the present perfect. 'Wrote' is simple past, 'writes' is simple present, and 'is writing' is present continuous.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Articles — A, An and The
lessons.notes_html:
The Three Articles

  • a — before a singular noun beginning with a consonant sound: a book, a school, a boy.
  • an — before a singular noun beginning with a vowel sound: an apple, an umbrella, an honest man (h is silent).
  • the — before a particular, known noun, or a unique thing: the sun, the moon, the Quran, the door of the room.

Rules from the Exercises

  • Use a/an when we mention something for the first time: "I saw a dog. The dog was black." (Second mention takes 'the'.)
  • Use the with names of rivers, seas, holy books and unique things: the Indus, the sun.
  • Use no article before proper nouns and general things: Pakistan, English (language), school subjects.
  • Sound matters, not the letter: a university (yoo-sound), an hour (silent h), a European.

Examples

  • She is an honest girl.
  • He bought a new car.
  • The sun rises in the east.
  • I read the Holy Quran every morning.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'She is ______ honest girl.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'an'. 'Honest' begins with a silent 'h', so its first sound is a vowel sound — and 'an' is used before vowel sounds.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'He bought ______ new car yesterday.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'a'. 'Car' begins with a consonant sound and is mentioned for the first time, so we use 'a'.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: '______ sun rises in the east.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'The'. The sun is a unique thing — there is only one — so it always takes 'the'.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'I saw ______ dog in the street. ______ dog was black.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'a / The'. At the first mention we use 'a dog'; when the same dog is mentioned again, it is now known, so we use 'the dog'.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'Please wait for ______ hour.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'an'. In 'hour' the letter h is silent, so the word starts with a vowel sound — sound, not spelling, decides between a and an.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'He studies in ______ university.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'a'. 'University' is pronounced 'yoo-niversity' — it begins with a consonant (y) sound, so 'a' is used even though the first letter is a vowel.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: '______ Indus is a long river.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'The'. Names of rivers take 'the': the Indus, the Chenab, the Nile.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: '______ English is an easy language.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is no article. Names of languages are used without an article when we speak of the language in general.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'She ate ______ apple and ______ banana.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'an / a'. 'Apple' starts with a vowel sound (an apple), while 'banana' starts with a consonant sound (a banana).

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'I read ______ Holy Quran every morning.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'the'. Names of holy books take 'the', like other unique and well-known things: the Holy Quran, the Bible.

lessons.title: Writing: E-mails
lessons.notes_html:
Writing an E-mail

An e-mail is a letter sent through the internet. It is quick and cheap. Every e-mail has these parts:

  • To — the e-mail address of the person receiving it.
  • Subject — one short line saying what the e-mail is about.
  • Greeting — Dear Ahmed, / Assalam-o-Alaikum, (for friends and family).
  • Body — the message, in short paragraphs.
  • Closing — Your friend, / Yours sincerely, + your name.

Model E-mail (to a friend)

  • To: ahmed@example.com
  • Subject: My visit to Mohenjo-Daro
  • Dear Ahmed,
  • Assalam-o-Alaikum. I hope you are fine. Last week our class visited Mohenjo-Daro. It was a wonderful trip. We saw the Great Bath and the Stupa. I wish you were with us.
  • Please write back soon and tell me about your holidays.
  • Your friend,
    Ali

Rules to Remember

  • Keep the subject short and clear.
  • Use polite language, just as in a letter.
  • Check the address carefully before sending — one wrong letter sends it to the wrong person.
  • Formal e-mails (to teachers or offices) use 'Respected Sir/Madam' and 'Yours sincerely/faithfully'.

mcqs.q: What is an e-mail?
options: A letter sent through the internet
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a letter sent through the internet. Writing 5.4 teaches e-mail writing — an e-mail reaches the other person in seconds and costs almost nothing.

mcqs.q: Where do we write what the e-mail is about, in one short line?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the subject line. A clear subject — like 'My visit to Mohenjo-Daro' — tells the reader the topic before opening the e-mail.

mcqs.q: In which part do we write the receiver's e-mail address?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'To'. The 'To' line carries the address of the person who will receive the e-mail.

mcqs.q: Which greeting suits an e-mail to a friend?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Dear Ahmed,'. Friendly e-mails begin with 'Dear' + the friend's name, while 'Respected Sir' is for formal e-mails to teachers or officers.

mcqs.q: Which closing suits the model e-mail to a friend?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Your friend, Ali'. The model e-mail ends with the closing 'Your friend' followed by the writer's name.

mcqs.q: In the model e-mail, what is the subject?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'My visit to Mohenjo-Daro'. The subject matches the body, which describes the class trip to Mohenjo-Daro, the Great Bath and the Stupa.

mcqs.q: What does the writer tell about in the body of the model e-mail?
options: The class visit to Mohenjo-Daro — the Great Bath and the Stupa
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the class visit to Mohenjo-Daro. The body says: 'Last week our class visited Mohenjo-Daro... We saw the Great Bath and the Stupa.'

mcqs.q: Why must we check the e-mail address carefully before sending?
options: One wrong letter can send it to the wrong person
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that one wrong letter can send it to the wrong person. An e-mail address must be exact, letter by letter, or the message will not reach the right person.

mcqs.q: Which is a formal closing for an e-mail to a teacher?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Yours sincerely'. Formal e-mails to teachers or offices open with 'Respected Sir/Madam' and close with 'Yours sincerely' or 'Yours faithfully'.

mcqs.q: What is the correct order of an e-mail's parts?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is To → Subject → Greeting → Body → Closing. Every part has its fixed place, as in the model e-mail of this unit.

lessons.title: Study Skills: Referring to and Reading a Content Page
lessons.notes_html:
What Is a Contents Page?

Every book has a contents page near the beginning. It lists the chapters or topics of the book with their page numbers, so we can find any topic quickly without turning every page.

A Sample Contents Page (Tourist Guide)

  • Castles — pages 18–21
  • Forts — pages 22–26
  • Tombs — pages 27–32
  • Museums — pages 38–43
  • Nature Walks — pages 68–72
  • Beaches — pages 78–82
  • Hotels and Restaurants — pages 87–93

How to Use It

  • To read about a topic, find it in the contents list and note its first page.
  • The topic continues until the page before the next topic begins.
  • For example: Beaches are on pages 78–82, Museums on 38–43, Tombs on 27–32, Hotels and Restaurants on 87–93, Nature Walks on 68–72, and Castles on 18–21 (Forts follow on 22–26).

Remember

Reading the contents page first gives us a map of the whole book. Good readers always check it before starting a book.

mcqs.q: What does a contents page show?
options: The chapters or topics of the book with their page numbers
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the chapters or topics with their page numbers. Study Skills 5.5 teaches us to refer to a contents page to find any topic quickly.

mcqs.q: On which pages is the topic 'Beaches' in the sample contents page?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is pages 78–82. The exercises ask for the page numbers of Beaches from the contents page, and the list gives Beaches — 78–82.

mcqs.q: On which pages is the topic 'Museums'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is pages 38–43. Reading the contents list: Castles 18–21, Forts 22–26, Tombs 27–32, Museums 38–43.

mcqs.q: Which topic is on pages 27–32?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Tombs. The contents page lists Tombs — pages 27–32, between Forts (22–26) and Museums (38–43).

mcqs.q: On which pages will you find 'Hotels and Restaurants'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is pages 87–93. This is the last topic in the sample contents list, and the exercise answer confirms it.

mcqs.q: On which pages is the topic 'Nature Walks'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is pages 68–72, as given in the contents page and confirmed by the exercise answers.

mcqs.q: Which topic begins on page 18?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Castles (pages 18–21). It is the first topic in the sample contents page; Forts follow it on pages 22–26.

mcqs.q: A topic listed as 'pages 78–82' has how many pages?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is five pages: 78, 79, 80, 81 and 82. A page range in a contents list includes both the first and the last page numbers.

mcqs.q: Where is the contents page usually found in a book?
options: Near the beginning of the book
mcqs.why: The correct answer is near the beginning of the book. It comes before the chapters so that readers can plan their reading and find topics at once.

mcqs.q: Why is the contents page useful?
options: It helps us find any topic quickly without turning every page
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that it helps us find any topic quickly. That is the whole skill of this section: 'Referring to and reading a content page'.

lessons.title: Fun: Creativity — Shopping and Grouping Items
lessons.notes_html:
The Fun Activity — Shopping

You and your friend are given a shopping list. You buy the items and put them into bags, grouping similar things together — for example, all the food items in one bag, toiletries in another, and so on.

The Shopping (Model)

  • The total cost of all the items bought was Rs 3,625.
  • The items were put into five bags.

Why Group Items?

  • Grouping keeps heavy and light things separate, so soft things are not crushed.
  • Cold and fresh food stays together; soap and washing things stay away from food.
  • It is easier to unpack at home when similar things are in one bag.

Remember

Before shopping, make a list; after shopping, check the bill and add the prices to know the total you have spent.

mcqs.q: In the Fun activity, what do you and your friend do?
options: Buy items from a shopping list and put them into bags, grouping similar things together
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to buy items from a shopping list and group them into bags. The activity is titled 'Creativity' in Fun 5.6, and the answers record the shopping's total and the number of bags.

mcqs.q: What was the total cost of all the items bought?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Rs 3,625. This is the total recorded in the exercise answer — pupils add up all the prices on the shopping list to reach it.

mcqs.q: Into how many bags were the items put?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is five bags. Similar items were grouped together until all the shopping fitted into five bags.

mcqs.q: Why do we group similar items in one bag?
options: So that soft things are not crushed and food stays away from soap and washing things
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to protect the items: heavy and light things are separated, and food is kept away from soap. Grouping also makes unpacking at home easier.

mcqs.q: Which items should be grouped together in one bag?
