options: Eggs with heavy tins on top
mcqs.why: The correct answer is all food items together. In the activity, items are sorted by kind — food in one bag, toiletries in another — so nothing spoils anything else.

mcqs.q: What should you do before going shopping, as the activity teaches?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to make a shopping list. The activity begins from a given shopping list — a list keeps us from forgetting items and from buying useless things.

mcqs.q: After shopping, how do we know the total spent?
options: By asking the shopkeeper next week
By adding up the prices of all the items (here, Rs 3,625)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is by adding up the prices. The recorded total of this shopping is Rs 3,625, which is the sum of every item's price.

mcqs.q: Heavy tins should be placed ______ in a bag.
options: at the bottom, with light things on top
mcqs.why: The correct answer is at the bottom, with light things on top. This grouping and packing sense is what the Fun activity practises — heavy things at the bottom cannot crush soft items.

mcqs.q: If two shoppers share the total bill of Rs 3,625 equally, the activity's main skill is still ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is grouping and organising things sensibly. The whole Fun task — sorting a mixed shopping list into five well-grouped bags — is an organising skill, like the contents page and the classification exercises of this book.

mcqs.q: Which pair is correctly grouped?
options: Milk and washing powder in one bag
Soap and sugar in one bag
Fruits and vegetables in one bag
mcqs.why: The correct answer is fruits and vegetables in one bag. They are the same kind of item (fresh food), while milk must stay away from washing powder and sugar from soap — the rule of the activity.

chapters.title: Media as a Source of Knowledge

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: Different Newspaper News
lessons.notes_html:
About the Lesson

In this lesson we read five news items from different newspapers. A piece of news tells us who, what, where, when and why. Each news item has a headline, the name of the agency or reporter, and the date.

News Item 1 — Three Children Drown (Mirpurkhas)

  • Three children drowned while bathing in a pond near Jhuddo town, Mirpurkhas — a very sad news.
  • Aqib (13) slipped into the deep water; his brother Suleman (11) and cousin Sajjid (10) jumped in to save him, but all three died.
  • Divers recovered the bodies; the children were buried in their native graveyard. Such accidents happen in the summer season, when children bathe in ponds and canals — parents should take care of their children.

News Item 2 — Children's Literature Festival (Islamabad)

  • The two-day Children's Literature Festival concluded at the Lok Virsa Museum, Islamabad — a happy and colourful news.
  • Children from public and private schools of the twin cities took part; there were storytelling sessions, book launches, workshops and puppet shows. Fines were imposed on some shopkeepers (in the matching exercise this belongs to the market news sense of rules) — the festival promoted reading habits among children.

News Item 3 — Zoo in Bahawalpur

  • A zoo in Bahawalpur looks after the animals well (its director was spoken to). A lion with his cubs was seen there — the exercises identify the animal as the lion (seen with three cubs; some sentences in the matching exercise are false, e.g. 'The tiger lives in the forest' as a wrong sentence about this item).

News Item 4 — Dengue Awareness Walk (Timergara)

  • A walk against dengue fever was held in Timergara. Students, teachers and health workers marched with banners.
  • People were told how dengue spreads (through mosquito bites) and how to prevent it — keep surroundings clean and do not let water stand.

News Item 5 — Fire at a Filling Station (Rawalpindi)

  • A fire broke out at a gas filling station in Rawalpindi. Firefighters reached quickly and controlled the fire; thankfully, lives were saved, though there was some loss.

Vocabulary to Know

  • drown — to die under water
  • conclude — to finish, come to an end
  • impose fine — to charge money as punishment
  • agency — a news organisation that collects and sends news (like APP)
  • dateline — the place and date written at the start of a news item

mcqs.q: How many news items are read in this lesson?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is five. The exercises work through five different newspaper items: Mirpurkhas (drowning accident), Islamabad (Children's Literature Festival), Bahawalpur (zoo), Timergara (dengue walk) and Rawalpindi (fire at a filling station).

mcqs.q: What sad news comes from Mirpurkhas?
options: Three children drowned while bathing in a pond
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that three children drowned. Aqib (13) slipped into deep water in a pond near Jhuddo town; Suleman (11) and Sajjid (10) jumped in to save him, but all three died.

mcqs.q: How did Suleman and Sajjid die?
options: They jumped into the pond to save their brother/cousin and drowned too
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that they jumped in to save Aqib and drowned too. It is a lesson for everyone: children must not bathe in deep ponds and canals without elders, especially in the summer season.

mcqs.q: Who recovered the bodies of the children?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is divers. The news says divers recovered the bodies, and the children were later buried in their native graveyard.

mcqs.q: Where was the Children's Literature Festival held?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Lok Virsa Museum, Islamabad. The two-day festival was held there and children from schools of the twin cities (Islamabad and Rawalpindi) took part.

mcqs.q: Which activities were part of the Children's Literature Festival?
options: Storytelling sessions, book launches, workshops and puppet shows
mcqs.why: The correct answer is storytelling sessions, book launches, workshops and puppet shows. The festival was held to promote reading habits and love of books among children.

mcqs.q: The word 'concluded' in the festival news means ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'came to an end'. The news begins: 'The two-day Children's Literature Festival concluded at the Lok Virsa Museum...' — a two-day event that has finished.

mcqs.q: Which animal is the Bahawalpur Zoo news about?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a lion. The exercises identify the zoo animal as the lion with his cubs, and one of the false matching sentences wrongly calls it a tiger.

mcqs.q: What was the Timergara news about?
options: An awareness walk against dengue fever
mcqs.why: The correct answer is an awareness walk against dengue fever. Students, teachers and health workers marched in Timergara to tell people how dengue spreads and how to prevent it.

mcqs.q: How can dengue be prevented, according to the walk's message?
options: By keeping surroundings clean and not letting water stand where mosquitoes breed
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to keep surroundings clean and not let water stand. Dengue spreads through mosquito bites, and mosquitoes breed in standing water — that was the awareness message of the Timergara walk.

mcqs.q: What happened in Rawalpindi in the fifth news item?
options: A fire broke out at a gas filling station and firefighters controlled it
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that a fire broke out at a gas filling station and firefighters controlled it. Fire news always tells where it happened, how it was controlled and what the loss was.

mcqs.q: What information does every good news item give?
options: Who, what, where, when and why
mcqs.why: The correct answer is who, what, where, when and why — the five W's. For example, the Mirpurkhas news tells who (three children), what (drowned), where (a pond near Jhuddo town) and when (in the summer bathing season).

mcqs.q: What is a 'dateline' in a news item?
options: The place and date written at the start of the news
The last line of the news
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the place and date at the start of the news, for example 'MIRPURKHAS: ...' News agencies like APP send news with a dateline so readers know where and when it happened.

mcqs.q: Which headline suits the festival news?
options: 'Children's Literature Festival Concludes at Lok Virsa'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Children's Literature Festival Concludes at Lok Virsa'. A headline must match its own news item — the other three headlines belong to the Mirpurkhas, Rawalpindi and Timergara items.

mcqs.q: What lesson do we learn from the Mirpurkhas news?
options: Parents should take care of their children, and children should not bathe in deep ponds and canals
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that parents should take care of their children and children should not bathe in deep ponds and canals. The news analysis notes that such sad accidents happen every summer for this reason.

lessons.title: Speaking: Expressing Disappointment
lessons.notes_html:
What We Practise

In section 6.2 we practise expressing disappointment. Disappointment is the sad feeling we get when something we hoped for does not happen.

Model Situations

  • Your friend promised to bring his cricket bat, but he forgot it. You say: "Oh no! I am so disappointed. We cannot play our match now."
  • You worked hard for the test but did not get the marks you expected. You say: "I am really disappointed with my result. I expected much better."
  • The class trip was cancelled because of rain. You say: "What a disappointment! We were all so excited about the trip."
  • Your team lost the final match. You say: "We are disappointed, but we will try harder next time."

Expressions of Disappointment

  • I am so disappointed.
  • What a disappointment!
  • That is really disappointing.
  • I expected much better.
  • Oh no! That is sad news.

Remember

Express disappointment politely — do not shout or blame others rudely. Like the last example shows, a good speaker also adds hope: "We will try harder next time."

mcqs.q: What speaking skill is practised in section 6.2?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is expressing disappointment. The section title is 'Speaking: Express Disappointment' — the sad feeling when something we hoped for does not happen.

mcqs.q: Your friend forgot to bring his cricket bat as promised. Which reply expresses disappointment?
options: Oh no! I am so disappointed. We cannot play our match now.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Oh no! I am so disappointed. We cannot play our match now.' The plan has failed, so disappointment — not happiness — is the right feeling to express.

mcqs.q: You got fewer marks than you expected in the test. Which sentence fits?
options: I am so happy with my result!
I am really disappointed with my result. I expected much better.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'I am really disappointed with my result. I expected much better.' 'I expected much better' is one of the book's disappointment expressions for results below our hopes.

mcqs.q: The class trip was cancelled because of rain. Which expression suits the situation?
options: What a disappointment! We were all so excited about the trip.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'What a disappointment! We were all so excited about the trip.' A cancelled trip is a classic disappointment situation; compare Unit 4, where going on a trip was happy surprise news.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an expression of disappointment?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'That is really disappointing.' All the other options express happiness or pleasure, while 'disappointing' names the sad feeling of unfulfilled hope.

mcqs.q: Your team lost the final match. Which reply is the best model of polite disappointment?
options: It is all the referee's fault, shout at him!
We are disappointed, but we will try harder next time.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'We are disappointed, but we will try harder next time.' Good speakers express disappointment politely without blaming or shouting, and they add hope for the future.

mcqs.q: Disappointment is felt when ______.
options: something we hoped for does not happen
mcqs.why: The correct answer is when something we hoped for does not happen. All the model situations — a forgotten bat, low marks, a cancelled trip, a lost final — share this one idea.

mcqs.q: Which sentence expresses disappointment at sad news from a friend?
options: Oh no! That is sad news. I am so disappointed to hear it.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Oh no! That is sad news. I am so disappointed to hear it.' It combines the surprise of bad news with the disappointment the section teaches.

mcqs.q: Which expression does NOT belong to disappointment?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'We've won!' That is an expression of happy surprise (Unit 4), the opposite feeling. The other three are all disappointment expressions from this section.

mcqs.q: Why should disappointment be expressed politely?
options: Because shouting or blaming others rudely does not change the result and hurts people
mcqs.why: The correct answer is because rudeness does not change the result and hurts people. The model answers express the feeling honestly but politely, and end with hope — 'we will try harder next time'.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Use of Since and For
lessons.notes_html:
Since and For with the Present Perfect

With the present perfect tense we use since and for to say how long something has continued:

  • since + a starting point in time: since 2010, since Monday, since morning, since 5 o'clock, since last year, since childhood.
  • for + a period (length) of time: for two hours, for five years, for a week, for a long time, for ten minutes.

Examples

  • I have lived in this city since 2015. / I have lived here for nine years.
  • She has been ill since Monday. / She has been ill for three days.
  • We have studied English since class one. / We have studied it for seven years.
  • It has been raining since morning. / It has rained for two hours.

The Golden Rule

Point of time → since. Period of time → for. Ask yourself: "Is it a point (a clock time, a day, a year, an event) or a length (how long)?"

Common Mistakes

  • ✗ since two hours → ✓ for two hours (a length)
  • ✗ for Monday → ✓ since Monday (a point)

mcqs.q: We use 'since' with ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a starting point in time. Since Monday, since 2010, since morning — each names the point from which something began and continues.

mcqs.q: We use 'for' with ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a period of time. For two hours, for five years, for a week — each tells how long, not when it started.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'I have lived in this city ______ 2015.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'since'. 2015 is a point in time — the starting point of living in the city — and points take 'since'.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'I have lived here ______ nine years.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'for'. Nine years is a length of time, and lengths take 'for'. Compare: 'since 2015' (point) and 'for nine years' (period) can describe the same stay.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'She has been ill ______ Monday.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'since'. Monday is a point in time, the day her illness started.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'She has been ill ______ three days.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'for'. Three days is a period — it answers 'how long?', which is the question 'for' answers.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'It has been raining ______ morning.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'since'. Morning is the starting point of the rain, and starting points take 'since' with the present perfect continuous.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'We have studied English ______ seven years.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'for'. Seven years is a period of time; if we name the starting point instead, we say 'since class one'.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: He has waited since two hours.
He has waited for two hours.
He has waited since a long time.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'He has waited for two hours.' Two hours is a period, so 'for' is correct; 'since two hours' and 'since a long time' wrongly use points, and 5 o'clock is a point that needs 'since'.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'They have played cricket ______ 4 o'clock.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'since'. 4 o'clock is an exact clock time — a point — so we say 'since 4 o'clock', but 'for two hours' for the length.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'My grandfather has lived in this village ______ a long time.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'for'. 'A long time' is a length, not a point, so it takes 'for' — a very common present-perfect phrase.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'She has known me ______ childhood.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'since'. Childhood is the starting point from which she has known me, and starting points take 'since'.

mcqs.q: Which pair is correct?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'since January / for five days'. January is a point in time and five days is a period — the golden rule of this lesson.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'The library has been closed ______ last Friday.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'since'. 'Last Friday' names the point when the closing began; a period answer would be 'for four days'.

mcqs.q: Which sentence uses since/for correctly?
options: I have not seen him for last month point.
I have not seen him since one month ago time.
I have not seen him for a month.
I have not seen him since a month.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'I have not seen him for a month.' A month here is a period of time, so 'for' is correct; 'since' would need a point like 'since last month' or 'since June'.

lessons.title: Writing: Narration of Requests and Orders — Direct and Indirect Speech
lessons.notes_html:
Direct and Indirect Speech — Requests and Orders

When we report what someone said, we can use their exact words (direct speech) or report the meaning in our own words (indirect/reported speech). In this unit we report requests and orders (imperative sentences).

The Rules

  • Use a reporting verb like asked, requested, ordered, told, advised + the person.
  • Join the order with to + verb: "Open the door" → He ordered the servant to open the door.
  • For a negative order, use not to: "Do not make a noise" → The teacher told the students not to make a noise.
  • Polite requests with 'please' become requested ... to: "Please help me" → She requested me to help her.
  • Pronouns change: me → him/her, my → his/her, as needed.

Examples

  • The captain said to the soldiers, "March forward." → The captain ordered the soldiers to march forward.
  • Mother said to me, "Do not go out in the rain." → Mother advised me not to go out in the rain.
  • The teacher said to the class, "Please submit your work." → The teacher requested the class to submit their work.

mcqs.q: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said to the students, 'Open your books.'
options: The teacher asked that open your books.
The teacher ordered students open the books.
The teacher ordered the students to open their books.
The teacher said the students to open books.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'The teacher ordered the students to open their books.' Orders are reported with ordered/told + person + to + verb, and 'your' becomes 'their'.

mcqs.q: Change into indirect speech: Mother said to me, 'Do not make a noise.'
options: Mother told me not to make a noise.
Mother told me to not making a noise.
Mother told me that do not make a noise.
Mother said me do not make a noise.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Mother told me not to make a noise.' Negative orders take 'not to' + verb in reported speech.

mcqs.q: Change into indirect speech: She said to me, 'Please help me.'
options: She requested me to help her.
She said please to help me.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'She requested me to help her.' A request with 'please' is reported with 'requested', and 'me' (the speaker) becomes 'her' from the reporter's view.

mcqs.q: Change into indirect speech: The captain said to the soldiers, 'March forward.'
options: The captain said soldiers to marching.
The captain ordered the soldiers to march forward.
The captain told the soldiers march forward.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'The captain ordered the soldiers to march forward.' A captain gives orders, so 'ordered' is the right reporting verb, followed by 'to march'.

mcqs.q: Change into indirect speech: The doctor said to the patient, 'Take rest.'
options: The doctor told to the patient to took rest.
The doctor advised the patient to take rest.
The doctor said patient take rest.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'The doctor advised the patient to take rest.' Advice from a doctor is reported with 'advised' + person + to + verb.

mcqs.q: Change into indirect speech: Father said to Ali, 'Do not waste your time.'
options: Father told Ali to not wasted his time.
Father advised Ali not to waste his time.
Father said Ali do not waste time.
Father told Ali that not waste your time.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Father advised Ali not to waste his time.' 'Not to' carries the negative order, and 'your' changes to 'his'.

mcqs.q: Which reporting verb best fits a polite request with 'please'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'requested'. 'Please' shows politeness, so the reported form uses 'requested ... to ...', while 'ordered' is for commands from authority.

mcqs.q: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said to us, 'Please submit your work.'
options: The teacher requested us to submit our work.
The teacher ordered us submit work.
The teacher requested us submitted our work.
The teacher said us please submit.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'The teacher requested us to submit our work.' Requested + us + to submit — and 'your' from the class's side becomes 'our' as we report it.

mcqs.q: In reported imperatives, the joining word before the verb is ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'to'. Reported orders and requests use the to-infinitive: told him to go, asked her to wait, ordered them not to shout.

mcqs.q: Change into indirect speech: He said to the servant, 'Bring me a glass of water.'
options: He ordered servant bringing him water.
He ordered the servant to bring him a glass of water.
He told the servant that bring me a glass of water.
He said servant bring me water.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'He ordered the servant to bring him a glass of water.' 'Me' (the speaker) becomes 'him' in the report, and the order is joined with 'to bring'.

lessons.title: Study Skills: Blurbs — Choosing the Right Book
lessons.notes_html:
Choosing a Book by Its Blurb

In Unit 4 we learnt that a blurb is the short text on a book's cover. In this unit we use blurbs to choose the right book — for ourselves or for a younger reader.

How a Blurb Helps Us Choose

  • It names the main character and the kind of story — adventure, funny, animal story, mystery.
  • It tells the age group the book suits.
  • Exciting lines make us curious, but we should check whether the story matches our interest.

Matching Books to Readers

  • A blurb about a boy and his animal friends suits a child who loves animals.
  • A blurb full of jokes and funny accidents suits a reader who wants to laugh.
  • A blurb about sports heroes suits a reader interested in games.

Remember the Practice Reminders

  • Do free writing regularly — it improves writing skills.
  • Practise cloze passages — useful for grammar and vocabulary.
  • Do loud reading every day — it develops spoken language.
  • Use the contents page to find topics quickly (Unit 5).

mcqs.q: In this unit, blurbs are used to ______.
options: choose the right book to read
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to choose the right book to read. Study Skills 6.5 returns to blurbs (first learnt in Unit 4) and uses them as a choosing tool.

mcqs.q: What does a good blurb tell us first?
options: The main character and the kind of story
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the main character and the kind of story. From James Trotter's blurb in Unit 4 we learnt the hero's name and the strange event that starts his adventure.

mcqs.q: A blurb about a boy and his animal friends best suits a reader who ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a reader who loves animals. Matching the blurb's subject to the reader's interest is exactly the choosing skill of this section.

mcqs.q: Why does a blurb mention the age group of readers?
options: So that we can pick a book suitable for the reader's age
mcqs.why: The correct answer is so that we can pick a book suitable for the reader's age. A Class 7 pupil choosing a book for a small child uses the blurb's age guidance.

mcqs.q: Which question should we ask before buying a book after reading its blurb?
options: Is the story of the kind I like, and is it right for my age?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is whether the story matches our interest and age. A blurb is written to attract us, but the wise reader checks the match before choosing.

mcqs.q: The blurb is found ______.
options: on the cover of the book
mcqs.why: The correct answer is on the cover of the book. Unit 4's exercise began: 'Read the cover page of the book written by Roald Dahl... According to the blurb...'

mcqs.q: Which reminder belongs to this book's study skills?
options: Do loud reading every day — it develops spoken language.
Read only the blurb, never the book.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to do loud reading every day. This reminder — with free writing for writing skills and cloze practice for grammar and vocabulary — runs through the study-skills sections of Units 4 to 6.

mcqs.q: A friend wants a funny book. Which blurb should you choose for him?
options: One describing jokes and funny accidents
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the one describing jokes and funny accidents. Choosing by blurb means matching the book's promised content to what the reader wants.

mcqs.q: What did the blurb of 'James and the Giant Peach' promise the reader?
options: A history of London Zoo only
An adventure of a boy whose parents were eaten by an escaped rhinoceros
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the adventure of James Trotter, whose parents were eaten by an enormous escaped rhinoceros from London Zoo. Such surprising details in a blurb make readers want the book.

mcqs.q: Which set of study skills has this book taught so far?
options: Free writing, cloze passages, dictionary use, blurbs and contents pages
mcqs.why: The correct answer is free writing, cloze passages, dictionary use, blurbs and contents pages. These are the Study Skills sections of Units 1 to 6 — skills for learning on our own.

lessons.title: Fun: Creativity — Who, What, Where, When, Why
lessons.notes_html:
The Fun Activity — Who, What, Where, When, Why

The Fun section gives information in a table about two world events for special players, and asks questions using the five question words: Who, What, Where, When, Why.

The Two Events

  • Street Child World Cup — a football event for street children, who often have no home or family support; it gives them a chance to play, be seen and speak for their rights.
  • Blind Cricket World Cup — a cricket event for blind players; it shows that blind people can play sports at world level with skill and courage.

Asking the Five Questions

  • Who plays in it? — Street children / blind cricketers.
  • What is it? — A world cup (football / cricket tournament).
  • Where and When is it held? — As given in the table for each event.
  • Why is it held? — To give special players a chance, to create awareness and to include them in sports.

Remember

These events connect with Unit 4's theme: special people should be included and respected. Sport gives them confidence and shows the world their abilities.

mcqs.q: Which two events are given in the Fun section's table?
options: The Hockey World Cup and the Asian Games
A school sports day and a quiz
The Street Child World Cup and the Blind Cricket World Cup
The Football World Cup and the Olympics
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Street Child World Cup and the Blind Cricket World Cup. The table gives information about these two events, and pupils answer Who/What/Where/When/Why questions from it.

mcqs.q: Who plays in the Street Child World Cup?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is street children. The event is specially for children who live on the streets, giving them a world stage in football.

mcqs.q: Who plays in the Blind Cricket World Cup?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is blind cricketers. Like the blind boy of Unit 4, these players show that blindness does not stop a person from achieving great things — even a world cup.

mcqs.q: Which question word asks about the reason for an event?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Why'. The five question words of the table are Who (person), What (thing/event), Where (place), When (time) and Why (reason).

mcqs.q: Why is the Street Child World Cup held?
options: To give street children a chance to play, be seen and speak for their rights
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to give street children a chance to play, be seen and speak for their rights. Such events create awareness about children who have no home or family support.

mcqs.q: Why is the Blind Cricket World Cup important?
options: It shows that blind people can play sports at world level with skill and courage
It is only for fun of the crowd
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that it shows blind people can play sports at world level. This is the empathy message of the whole book: special people deserve inclusion and respect.

mcqs.q: Which question word asks about a place?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Where'. In the table questions — Who plays, What is it, Where is it held, When is it held, Why is it held — each word has its own job.

mcqs.q: What is the Street Child World Cup (What)?
options: A football tournament for street children
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a football tournament for street children. Answering 'What is it?' from the table identifies the event itself, just as 'Who' identifies its players.

mcqs.q: What is the Blind Cricket World Cup (What)?
options: A cricket tournament for blind players
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a cricket tournament for blind players. Blind cricket is played with a ball that makes a sound, so players can follow it by hearing.

mcqs.q: How do these two events connect with Unit 4 of this book?
options: They are both about ancient places
They teach empathy and inclusion for special people, like the poem 'The Blind Boy'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that they teach empathy and inclusion for special people. Unit 4 ('Awareness of and Empathy with Special People') and this Fun table carry the same message: respect abilities, do not pity.

chapters.title: Learning Organized Approach through Identifying, Prioritizing, and Following Schedules

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: Rafia's Wedding — A Play
lessons.notes_html:
About the Lesson

"Rafia's Wedding" is a small play (drama) in two scenes. It teaches us how to plan and organise an event — the main theme of this unit: identifying work, prioritising it and following a schedule.

The Story

  • Rafia's wedding is near. There is a lot of work to do: food, clothes, guests, decoration and the hall.
  • An accident happens: Jawad's father has broken his leg. He is taken to the Bhitai Hospital.
  • The doctor says the leg must be in a cast (plaster) for six weeks.
  • The family is worried — how will all the wedding work be done now?
  • Hassan comes forward to help the family with the arrangements.
  • The family plans the food carefully and keeps the budget in mind: the food budget is Rs 20,000.
  • Working together, following the plan and the schedule, everything is ready on time and the wedding takes place happily.

Key Points

  • A budget is a plan of how money will be spent. Planning the budget stops waste.
  • When trouble comes, family and friends should help each other — Hassan's help saves the wedding work.
  • Organised work = list the tasks, decide which are most important (prioritise), fix times (schedule), and follow the plan.

Word Meanings

  • cast — hard plaster covering put on a broken bone
  • budget — a plan for spending money
  • arrangements — preparations for an event
  • prioritise — to decide what is most important and do it first
  • schedule — a plan of times for doing things

mcqs.q: What kind of text is 'Rafia's Wedding'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a play (drama) in two scenes. The reading text is written as scenes with characters speaking — pupils can even act it out in class.

mcqs.q: What problem does the family face before the wedding?
options: Jawad's father has broken his leg
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that Jawad's father has broken his leg. With an important family member injured, the family worries how all the wedding arrangements will be completed.

mcqs.q: To which hospital is Jawad's father taken?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Bhitai Hospital. The play names the hospital where the doctor treats his broken leg.

mcqs.q: For how long must the broken leg stay in a cast?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is six weeks. The doctor at Bhitai Hospital says the leg must remain in a cast (plaster) for six weeks while the bone heals.

mcqs.q: Who comes forward to help the family with the wedding arrangements?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hassan. His help shows the family's unity — when one member cannot work, another steps in, which is also the play's lesson in cooperation.

mcqs.q: What is the food budget for the wedding?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Rs 20,000. The family discusses the food arrangements carefully and fixes this budget — planning money is part of organising any event, the theme of this unit.

mcqs.q: What does 'budget' mean?
options: A plan of how money will be spent
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a plan of how money will be spent. In the play the family keeps the food budget of Rs 20,000 in mind while deciding the menu.

mcqs.q: What is a 'cast' in this lesson?
options: Hard plaster covering put on a broken bone
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the hard plaster put on a broken bone. Note the word's other meaning — the actors of a play — but here, with a broken leg and 'six weeks', it clearly means the plaster.

mcqs.q: What is the main lesson of the play?
options: With planning, prioritising, a schedule and mutual help, work is completed on time
We should cancel events when trouble comes
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that planning, prioritising, a schedule and mutual help complete the work on time. That is the unit's title idea: 'Learning Organized Approach through Identifying, Prioritizing, and Following Schedules'.

mcqs.q: What does 'prioritise' mean?
options: To decide what is most important and do it first
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to decide what is most important and do it first. The wedding family first arranges the essentials — food, hall, guests — before smaller things.

mcqs.q: Why does the family discuss the food budget carefully?
options: So that money is not wasted and spending stays within Rs 20,000
mcqs.why: The correct answer is so that money is not wasted. A budget keeps spending inside the fixed amount — the same careful planning the unit teaches for studies and daily life.

mcqs.q: How does the play end?
options: The family moves to another city
Jawad's father leaves the hospital after a year
Everything is ready on time and the wedding takes place happily
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that everything is ready on time and the wedding takes place happily. Organised work and Hassan's help overcome the accident's problem — the satisfying end of the drama.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an 'arrangement' for a wedding?
options: Booking the hall and preparing the food
mcqs.why: The correct answer is booking the hall and preparing the food. Arrangements are the preparations for an event — food, hall, clothes, guests and decoration in this play.

mcqs.q: What should a family do first when an event is near, according to this unit?
options: List all the tasks, prioritise them and make a schedule
Spend all the money on clothes
Invite guests on the last day
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to list tasks, prioritise them and make a schedule. This 'organised approach' is the unit's title and the play's working method.

mcqs.q: Jawad's father broke his leg. This accident teaches the family to ______.
options: share the work and help one another
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to share the work and help one another. Hassan takes over tasks, the family follows its plan, and the wedding succeeds — cooperation is the play's second big lesson.

lessons.title: Speaking: Asking and Answering Questions of Personal Interest
lessons.notes_html:
What We Practise

In section 7.2 we practise asking and answering questions of personal interest — questions about a person's life, family, likes, dislikes, school and plans. This is how we interview someone or make a new friend talk about himself.

Useful Questions of Personal Interest

  • What is your full name?
  • Where do you live?
  • How many brothers and sisters do you have?
  • Which is your favourite subject? Why?
  • What is your hobby?
  • What do you want to become in the future?
  • Which game do you like most?
  • Who is your best friend?

Model Exchange

  • A: What is your hobby?
  • B: My hobby is reading storybooks. I read every evening.
  • A: Which is your favourite subject?
  • B: English is my favourite subject because I like stories and poems.
  • A: What do you want to become?
  • B: I want to become a teacher in the future.

Remember

  • Ask one question at a time and listen to the answer.
  • Answer in full sentences, not only "yes" or "no".
  • Be polite — personal questions should be friendly, never rude.

mcqs.q: What speaking skill is practised in section 7.2?
options: Asking and answering questions of personal interest
mcqs.why: The correct answer is asking and answering questions of personal interest. The section title is 'Speaking: Ask and answer of personal interest' — questions about a person's life, family, likes and plans.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a question of personal interest?
options: What is the capital of France?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'What is your hobby?' A hobby is personal — it belongs to the person's own life and interests, unlike general-knowledge questions.

mcqs.q: Which question asks about a person's family?
options: How many brothers and sisters do you have?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'How many brothers and sisters do you have?' Questions about family are classic personal-interest questions used in interviews and introductions.

mcqs.q: How should we answer a personal-interest question?
options: By asking the same question back only
In a full sentence, giving a little detail
mcqs.why: The correct answer is in a full sentence with a little detail, like 'My hobby is reading storybooks. I read every evening.' Full answers keep the conversation alive and show good speaking skill.

mcqs.q: Which is a good follow-up after 'Which is your favourite subject?'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Why do you like it?' A follow-up question shows interest and gives the speaker a chance to explain, as in the model exchange: 'English is my favourite subject because I like stories and poems.'

mcqs.q: What do you want to become in the future?' — this question asks about ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the person's plans and ambition. Personal-interest questions can cover the past (childhood), present (hobbies) and future (aims), like the model answer 'I want to become a teacher.'

mcqs.q: While asking personal questions, we should ______.
options: ask one question at a time, listen politely and stay friendly
ask rude questions about private matters
ask many questions at once and not listen
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to ask one question at a time, listen politely and stay friendly. Personal questions must always be respectful — that is the manners point of this speaking section.

mcqs.q: Which question of personal interest fits a new classmate?
options: Where do you live, and which game do you like most?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Where do you live, and which game do you like most?' Both parts ask about the classmate's own life and likes — exactly 'personal interest'.

mcqs.q: In the model exchange, why does B like English?
options: Because he likes stories and poems
Because it is easy to copy
mcqs.why: The correct answer is because he likes stories and poems. Giving a reason after an answer — 'because...' — is the good-answer pattern taught in this section.

mcqs.q: Which answer is complete for 'What is your hobby?'
options: My hobby is reading storybooks, and I read every evening.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'My hobby is reading storybooks, and I read every evening.' It repeats the question words in a full sentence and adds a detail — the model style for this section.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Adverbs and Their Position
lessons.notes_html:
What Is an Adverb?

An adverb tells us more about a verb — how, when, where or how often an action is done. Many adverbs of manner end in -ly: slowly, carefully, happily, quietly.

Four Kinds (from the exercises)

  • How? (manner) — She sings beautifully. He runs fast.
  • When? (time) — We will go tomorrow. He came late.
  • Where? (place) — The children are playing outside. Come here.
  • How often? (frequency) — I always brush my teeth. She sometimes visits us.

Position of Adverbs

  • Adverbs of manner usually come after the verb or object: "He speaks English fluently."
  • Adverbs of frequency (always, usually, often, sometimes, never) come before the main verb: "I always get up early." But with the verb 'be' they come after it: "He is always late."
  • Adverbs of time often come at the beginning or end of a sentence: "Yesterday we went to the zoo." / "We went to the zoo yesterday."

Practice Sentences

  • The cap-seller slept soundly under the tree. (how)
  • The monkeys threw the caps down. (where)
  • He never tells a lie. (how often)

mcqs.q: An adverb tells us more about ______.
options: a verb — how, when, where or how often an action is done
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a verb. Adverbs answer How? When? Where? or How often? about the action — the four question groups practised in this lesson.

mcqs.q: In 'She sings beautifully', the adverb 'beautifully' answers ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'How?' She sings in a beautiful manner. Adverbs of manner like beautifully, slowly and carefully usually end in -ly.

mcqs.q: In 'We will go tomorrow', 'tomorrow' is an adverb of ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is time. It answers 'When will we go?' Adverbs of time (today, tomorrow, yesterday, now) often stand at the beginning or end of a sentence.

mcqs.q: In 'The children are playing outside', 'outside' answers ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Where?' Outside, here, there and upstairs are adverbs of place — they tell where the action happens.

mcqs.q: In 'I always brush my teeth', 'always' tells ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is how often — frequency. Always, usually, often, sometimes and never are adverbs of frequency, and they usually come before the main verb.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'He speaks English fluently.' An adverb of manner usually comes after the verb and its object — 'speaks English' first, then 'fluently'.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'He is always late.' With the verb 'be', the adverb of frequency comes after it: is + always. With other verbs it comes before: 'I always get up early.'

mcqs.q: Which word is an adverb?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'quickly'. Adding -ly to the adjective 'quick' makes the adverb of manner — the pattern of slowly, carefully and happily in this lesson.

mcqs.q: In 'The cap-seller slept soundly under the tree', 'soundly' tells ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is how he slept. 'Soundly' (deeply) describes the manner of sleeping; 'under the tree' answers where.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I tell never a lie in.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'I never tell a lie.' The frequency adverb 'never' stands before the main verb 'tell' — the standard position taught in this lesson.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Active Voice and Passive Voice
lessons.notes_html:
Active and Passive Voice

  • Active voice: the subject does the action — "Ali wrote a letter."
  • Passive voice: the action is done to the subject — "A letter was written by Ali."

The Rule for Changing

  • Object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive.
  • Use be (is/are/was/were) + past participle (3rd form) of the verb.
  • The doer comes after by (we may drop it if unknown or unimportant).
  • Simple present: Ali writes a letter → A letter is written by Ali.
  • Simple past: Ali wrote a letter → A letter was written by Ali.
  • Present continuous: She is cooking food → Food is being cooked by her.

News Blanks (from the storm report practice)

  • "Many trees were uprooted by the storm."
  • "Several houses were damaged."
  • "The roads were blocked by fallen trees."
  • News reports often use the passive because what happened matters more than who did it.

mcqs.q: Change into passive voice: 'Ali wrote a letter.'
options: A letter was written by Ali.
A letter is written by Ali.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'A letter was written by Ali.' The active verb 'wrote' is simple past, so the passive uses 'was' + past participle 'written'.

mcqs.q: Change into passive voice: 'She cooks food.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Food is cooked by her.' 'Cooks' is simple present, so we use 'is' + 'cooked', and 'she' becomes 'her' after 'by'.

mcqs.q: Change into passive voice: 'The boys are playing cricket.'
options: Cricket are being played by the boys.
Cricket is played by boys playing.
Cricket is being played by the boys.
Cricket was played by the boys.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Cricket is being played by the boys.' Present continuous active (are playing) becomes 'is being' + past participle, and 'cricket' is singular, so 'is', not 'are'.

mcqs.q: Change into passive voice: 'The storm uprooted many trees.'
options: Many trees were uprooted by the storm.
Many trees are uprooted by storm yesterday.
The storm was uprooted many trees.
Many trees uprooted by the storm.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Many trees were uprooted by the storm.' This is exactly the style of the storm news blanks in the exercises: plural subject 'trees' takes 'were' + 'uprooted'.

mcqs.q: Change into active voice: 'The thief was caught by the police.'
options: The police was caught the thief.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'The police caught the thief.' To make it active, the doer (the police) becomes the subject and 'was caught' returns to the simple past 'caught'.

mcqs.q: In a passive sentence, the verb is always ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is be + past participle. Is written, was written, are damaged, were blocked — every passive in this lesson follows this one pattern.

mcqs.q: Change into passive voice: 'We use since for a point of time.'
options: A point of time is used since.
Since was using for a point.
Since is used for a point of time (by us).
Since used by we for time.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Since is used for a point of time.' When the doer is unimportant, 'by us' is usually dropped — one of the main uses of the passive voice.

mcqs.q: Change into passive voice: 'The teacher punished the students.'
options: The students are punished by the teacher.
The teacher was punished the students.
The students punished by the teacher were.
The students were punished by the teacher.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'The students were punished by the teacher.' 'Punished' is past tense and 'students' is plural, so 'were' + 'punished' is correct.

mcqs.q: Why do news reports often use the passive voice?
options: Because what happened matters more than who did it
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that what happened matters more than who did it. In the storm report — 'houses were damaged', 'roads were blocked' — the event is the news, not the doer.

mcqs.q: Change into passive voice: 'They will announce the result tomorrow.'
options: The result will announced by them.
Tomorrow will be announced the result.
The result will be announced tomorrow (by them).
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'The result will be announced tomorrow.' Future passive = will be + past participle, following the same be + 3rd-form rule.

mcqs.q: Change into passive voice: 'Someone stole my bicycle.'
options: My bicycle is stole by someone.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'My bicycle was stolen.' The doer 'someone' is unknown, so it is dropped — a perfect use of the passive. 'Stolen' is the past participle of steal.

mcqs.q: Change into active voice: 'English is spoken all over the world.'
options: People speak English all over the world.
All over the world English speak.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'People speak English all over the world.' The passive hides the doer; in the active we supply 'people' as the subject and use the simple present 'speak'.

mcqs.q: Choose the passive sentence.
options: The mouse was chased by the cat.
The cat is chasing the mouse.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'The mouse was chased by the cat.' Was + chased (past participle) with the doer after 'by' marks the passive; the other sentences are active.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank (news style): 'Several houses ______ in the storm.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'were damaged'. A passive blank needs be + past participle, and 'houses' (plural, past event) takes 'were' — from the storm-report practice in the exercises.

mcqs.q: Change into passive voice: 'The doctor examined the patient.'
options: The doctor was examined the patient.
The patient examined by the doctor.
The patient is examining the doctor.
The patient was examined by the doctor.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'The patient was examined by the doctor.' The object 'the patient' becomes the subject, and 'examined' (past) becomes 'was examined'.

lessons.title: Writing: Descriptive Essay Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Descriptive Essay Writing

A descriptive essay describes a person, place or thing in words, so that the reader can see a picture of it in the mind. We describe appearance, qualities and habits using clear details.

Model Essay — 'My Teacher' (from the unit's writing work)

  • Introduction: My teacher's name is _______. He/She teaches us English in Class 7.
  • Appearance: He is tall and smart. He always wears clean clothes and has a kind face.
  • Qualities: He is punctual, honest and kind. He explains every lesson clearly and never gets angry without reason.
  • Habits and method: He comes to class on time, checks our homework daily and helps weak students after class.
  • Conclusion: All the students respect and love him. I want to become like my teacher in the future.

How to Write a Descriptive Essay

  • Paragraph 1 — introduce the person/place.
  • Paragraph 2 — describe the appearance.
  • Paragraph 3 — describe the qualities and habits with examples.
  • Last paragraph — your feelings and a conclusion.
  • Use describing words (adjectives): tall, kind, punctual, honest, helpful.

mcqs.q: What is a descriptive essay?
options: An essay that argues a point
An essay that tells a story with a moral
An essay that describes a person, place or thing so the reader can picture it
mcqs.why: The correct answer is an essay that describes a person, place or thing so the reader can picture it. Writing 7.4 is 'Descriptive Essay Writing', modelled by the essay 'My Teacher'.

mcqs.q: What comes in the first paragraph of the model essay 'My Teacher'?
options: The introduction of the teacher — name and subject taught
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the introduction of the teacher. A descriptive essay opens by presenting its subject before describing appearance and qualities.

mcqs.q: Which words are describing words (adjectives) for the teacher?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is tall, kind, punctual, honest and helpful. Description is built with adjectives — tall and smart for appearance; kind, honest and punctual for qualities.

mcqs.q: Which detail describes the teacher's habits and method?
options: He explains every lesson clearly and helps weak students after class.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that he explains every lesson clearly and helps weak students after class. Habits and method — what the person regularly does — form the third paragraph of the model essay.

mcqs.q: How does the model essay end?
options: With the writer's feelings — all students respect and love him, and the writer wants to become like him
mcqs.why: The correct answer is with the writer's feelings and a conclusion. Ending a descriptive essay with feelings ('I want to become like my teacher') completes the picture warmly.

mcqs.q: Describe in the right order: a descriptive essay's paragraphs are ______.
options: Introduction → appearance → qualities and habits → conclusion
mcqs.why: The correct answer is introduction → appearance → qualities and habits → conclusion. This fixed order keeps the description clear, exactly as the model essay is built.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is a true description sentence?
options: My teacher always reaches school on time and speaks politely to everyone.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the first sentence. It describes the teacher's regular habit and manner with details — the heart of descriptive writing — while the others are not descriptions of a person.

mcqs.q: Why do we give examples in a descriptive essay?
options: So the reader can clearly picture the person's qualities
mcqs.why: The correct answer is so the reader can clearly picture the qualities. Saying 'he is kind' is weak; adding 'he helps weak students after class' shows the kindness — description needs such details.

mcqs.q: Which topic can also be written as a descriptive essay in this style?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'My School'. Places, like persons, are described by appearance, special features and our feelings — the same plan as 'My Teacher'.

mcqs.q: Which sentence best describes a place?
options: Our school is a big building with green lawns, tall trees and bright classrooms.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the first sentence. It paints a picture with describing details — big building, green lawns, tall trees, bright classrooms — which is what descriptive writing means.

lessons.title: Study Skills: Use of Dictionary
lessons.notes_html:
Using the Dictionary — the Word 'Instinct'

In Unit 3 we learnt how to find a word in a dictionary (alphabetical order, guide words, parts of speech). Here we go deeper with one word and its family.

The Word Family of 'Instinct'

  • instinct (noun) — a natural feeling or power that makes a person or animal act in a certain way without thinking. Example: Birds build nests by instinct. A mother's instinct protects her child.
  • instinctive (adjective) — done by instinct, without thinking. Example: His instinctive reaction was to run.
  • instinctively (adverb) — in an instinctive way. Example: She instinctively held her child's hand in the crowd.

What a Dictionary Entry Shows

  • The word and its pronunciation.
  • Its part of speech (noun, adjective, adverb...).
  • Its meaning(s) in simple words.
  • An example sentence.
  • Related words of the same family (like instinctive and instinctively).

Remember

When you learn one word from the dictionary, also learn its family — one visit then gives you three words instead of one.

mcqs.q: What does the noun 'instinct' mean?
options: A natural feeling or power that makes a person or animal act in a certain way without thinking
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a natural feeling or power that makes us act without thinking. Study Skills 7.5 explores the word 'instinct': birds build nests by instinct, and a mother protects her child by instinct.

mcqs.q: 'Instinctive' is which part of speech?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is adjective. The dictionary family is: instinct (noun), instinctive (adjective), instinctively (adverb) — one root, three parts of speech.

mcqs.q: 'Instinctively' is which part of speech?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is adverb. The -ly ending is the clue: 'She instinctively held her child's hand' — it tells how she held the hand, exactly the adverb lesson of this unit.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Birds build nests an instinctive of.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Birds build nests by instinct.' After 'by' we need the noun 'instinct', not the adjective 'instinctive' — the dictionary family must be used with the right part of speech.

mcqs.q: What does a dictionary entry show us?
options: Pronunciation, part of speech, meanings, example sentences and related words
mcqs.why: The correct answer is pronunciation, part of speech, meanings, examples and related words. That is why the dictionary exercises of Units 3 and 7 ask for all of these from one entry.

mcqs.q: In 'His instinctive reaction was to run away', 'instinctive' describes ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the reaction (a noun). Adjectives describe nouns; 'instinctive' tells us what kind of reaction it was — one that came from instinct, without thinking.

mcqs.q: Why is it useful to learn a word's family from the dictionary?
options: One visit gives us several related words — noun, adjective and adverb
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that one visit gives several related words. Learning instinct, instinctive and instinctively together triples the value of a single dictionary look-up.

mcqs.q: Which word would come just before 'instinct' in a dictionary?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'insect'. Dictionary order is alphabetical: in-sect comes before in-stinct because 'e' (in 'se') comes before 't' (in 'st') at the deciding letters — the skill first taught in Unit 3.

mcqs.q: A mother's quick action to save her child from falling, without thinking, is an example of ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is instinct. Acting correctly and immediately without thinking first is the exact meaning of the word studied in this section.

mcqs.q: The guide words on a dictionary page help us to ______.
options: know quickly whether our word is on that page
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to know quickly whether our word is on that page. Guide words (the first and last words of the page) were taught with the 'collapse' exercise in Unit 3 and are used again here.

lessons.title: Fun: Poem — Why?
lessons.notes_html:
The Fun Section — the Poem 'Why?'

The Fun section of this unit gives a short poem full of a child's questions — all beginning with Why? Children ask why about everything around them, and good answers grow their knowledge.

The Boy's Questions (with model answers)

  • Why is the sky blue? — Because the air scatters the blue part of sunlight to our eyes.
  • Why does the sun rise in the east? — Because the Earth turns from west to east.
  • Why do birds fly? — Because they have wings and light, hollow bones.
  • Why does it rain? — Because water vapour in clouds cools, becomes drops and falls.
  • Why is the sea salty? — Because rivers carry salts from the land into the sea.

Remember

Asking 'why' is the beginning of learning. Never feel shy of asking questions — in this very book, question words (Unit 4) and the dictionary (Units 3 and 7) are tools for finding the answers.

mcqs.q: What is the Fun section of Unit 7?
options: A poem called 'Why?' full of a child's questions
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a poem called 'Why?'. The textbook's own table of contents lists Unit 7's Fun as 'Poem', and the poem is built from a child's wondering questions.

mcqs.q: Why is the sky blue, according to the model answer?
options: Because the sea reflects in it only
Because the air scatters the blue part of sunlight to our eyes
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that the air scatters the blue part of sunlight. This is the simple science answer given for the poem's first kind of question.

mcqs.q: Why does the sun rise in the east?
options: Because the Earth turns from west to east
The sun moves round the Earth daily
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that the Earth turns from west to east. The sun only appears to move; it is the Earth's turning that gives us sunrise in the east and sunset in the west.

mcqs.q: Why can birds fly?
options: Because they have wings and light, hollow bones
Because the wind always lifts them
Because they are very light only
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that birds have wings and light, hollow bones. Wings give the lift and hollow bones keep the body light — the model answer to the poem's question.

mcqs.q: Why does it rain?
options: Water vapour in clouds cools, becomes drops and falls as rain
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that water vapour cools and falls as drops. This is the water cycle in one line — evaporation, cooling, and rain.

mcqs.q: Why is the sea salty?
options: Rivers carry salts from the land into the sea
It was made so in one day
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that rivers carry salts from the land into the sea. Over ages the salts collect in the sea because the water evaporates but the salt stays.

mcqs.q: What does the poem teach us about asking questions?
options: Asking 'why' is the beginning of learning; never feel shy of asking
Questions are a waste of time
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that asking 'why' is the beginning of learning. This book itself trains the habit — question words in Unit 4 and dictionary skills in Units 3 and 7 exist so pupils can find answers.

mcqs.q: Which question word begins every question in the poem?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Why'. The poem's title is the question word itself, and every verse asks for a reason — matching the Fun table of Unit 6 (Who, What, Where, When, Why).

mcqs.q: A child asks, 'Why do we sleep at night?' Which is a good answer style?
options: 'Because our body and mind need rest to work well the next day.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the response that gives a true reason in simple words. The poem 'Why?' models exactly this: every curious question receives a clear, kind answer.

mcqs.q: How does the poem 'Why?' connect with the unit's theme of organised learning?
options: It does not connect at all
Poems are only for fun time
Curiosity and questions lead us to knowledge, which we then organise with schedules and plans
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that curiosity leads to knowledge, which we organise with schedules and plans. Unit 7 joins both: learn through questions (reading, speaking, dictionary) and manage learning through an organised approach.
